CONSTANTS Servers, Registrars, NoServer, MaxSeats

ASSUME NoServer \notin Servers

Stages == {"idle", "canvassing", "editing"}

VARIABLES vote, stage, override, seats, basis

vars == <<vote, stage, override, seats, basis>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ vote \in [Registrars -> Servers \cup {NoServer}]
    /\ stage \in [Servers -> Stages]
    /\ override \in Servers \cup {NoServer}
    /\ seats \in 0 .. MaxSeats
    /\ basis \in [Servers -> {"none", "quorum", "admin"}]

Init ==
    /\ vote = [r \in Registrars |-> NoServer]
    /\ stage = [s \in Servers |-> "idle"]
    /\ override = NoServer
    /\ seats = 0
    /\ basis = [s \in Servers |-> "none"]

Inside == {s \in Servers : stage[s] = "editing"}
Backers(s) == {r \in Registrars : vote[r] = s}
HasMandate(s) == 2 * Cardinality(Backers(s)) > Cardinality(Registrars)
Legitimate == {s \in Servers : basis[s] = "admin" \/ HasMandate(s)}

Canvass(s) ==
    /\ stage[s] = "idle"
    /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![s] = "canvassing"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<vote, override, seats, basis>>

Cast(r, s) ==
    /\ vote[r] = NoServer
    /\ stage[s] = "canvassing"
    /\ vote' = [vote EXCEPT ![r] = s]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stage, override, seats, basis>>

\* Backing is held for the duration of an edit, so no server loses its
\* mandate while it is still inside the ledger.
Retract(r) ==
    /\ vote[r] # NoServer
    /\ stage[vote[r]] # "editing"
    /\ vote' = [vote EXCEPT ![r] = NoServer]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stage, override, seats, basis>>

\* A standing override closes the quorum path entirely; entry records the
\* basis it was granted on, and that basis is what the invariant judges.
Enter(s) ==
    /\ Inside = {}
    /\ stage[s] # "editing"
    /\ \/ /\ override = s
          /\ basis' = [basis EXCEPT ![s] = "admin"]
       \/ /\ override = NoServer
          /\ stage[s] = "canvassing"
          /\ HasMandate(s)
          /\ basis' = [basis EXCEPT ![s] = "quorum"]
    /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![s] = "editing"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<vote, override, seats>>

Adjust(s, n) ==
    /\ stage[s] = "editing"
    /\ n \in 0 .. MaxSeats
    /\ n # seats
    /\ seats' = n
    /\ UNCHANGED <<vote, stage, override, basis>>

Leave(s) ==
    /\ stage[s] = "editing"
    /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![s] = "idle"]
    /\ basis' = [basis EXCEPT ![s] = "none"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<vote, override, seats>>

Override(s) ==
    /\ override = NoServer
    /\ stage[s] # "editing"
    /\ override' = s
    /\ UNCHANGED <<vote, stage, seats, basis>>

\* The office cannot take an override back until it has been honoured.
Clear(s) ==
    /\ override = s
    /\ stage[s] = "editing"
    /\ override' = NoServer
    /\ UNCHANGED <<vote, stage, seats, basis>>

Next ==
    \/ \E s \in Servers : Canvass(s)
    \/ \E r \in Registrars, s \in Servers : Cast(r, s)
    \/ \E r \in Registrars : Retract(r)
    \/ \E s \in Servers : Enter(s)
    \/ \E s \in Servers, n \in 0 .. MaxSeats : Adjust(s, n)
    \/ \E s \in Servers : Leave(s)
    \/ \E s \in Servers : Override(s)
    \/ \E s \in Servers : Clear(s)

Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(\E s \in Servers : Leave(s))
    /\ WF_vars(\E s \in Servers : Enter(s))

\* At most one server inside, and only ever one entitled to be there: an
\* admin entrant, or a quorum entrant that still holds its majority.
ExclusiveEntitledEditing ==
    /\ Inside \subseteq Legitimate
    /\ \A s1 \in Inside : \A s2 \in Inside : s1 = s2

OverrideIsHonoured ==
    \A s \in Servers : (override = s) ~> (stage[s] = "editing")

CONSTANTS
    Servers = {srvA, srvB}
    Registrars = {reg1, reg2, reg3}
    NoServer = noserver
    MaxSeats = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT ExclusiveEntitledEditing

PROPERTY OverrideIsHonoured
nl:
A university runs course registration on a small set of registration servers that all front the same seat ledger for a course. Editing that ledger is the critical section: exactly one server may be inside it at a time, because the ledger is read-modify-written and two servers inside it at once oversell the course.

There is no lock service. Instead a server that wants the ledger canvasses the faculty registrars for backing. Each registrar has one vote and may hold it uncommitted or commit it to one canvassing server. A registrar may not switch its vote directly: it must first retract, and it is not allowed to retract a vote from a server that is currently inside the ledger -- backing is held for the duration of the edit, which is what stops a server losing its mandate mid-edit. A server may enter the ledger on the strength of a strict majority of the registrars backing it, and only while no other server is inside.

Registration also has a privileged path. The registrar's office can assert an administrative override naming one server. While an override is standing, the quorum path is closed to everybody: no server can enter on votes, and only the named server may enter. The override also bypasses the per-server edit budget that otherwise caps how many times a server may take the ledger on its own mandate -- that budget exists to stop one server monopolising registration, and the override is precisely the escape hatch from it. The office cannot withdraw an override until the server it names has actually got inside the ledger, and it cannot name a new server while one override is still standing.

The full set of actions is: Canvass, in which an idle server starts canvassing; Cast, in which an uncommitted registrar commits its vote to a canvassing server; Retract, in which a registrar takes back a vote from a server that is not currently inside the ledger; Enter, in which a server enters the ledger, either because it is the server named by a standing override, or because no override is standing, it is canvassing, it has a strict majority of registrars behind it and edit budget left, in which case its budget is spent; Adjust, in which the server inside the ledger changes the seat count by one within the configured range; Leave, in which the server inside the ledger steps out and goes idle; Override, in which the registrar's office names a server while no override stands and that server is not already inside; and Clear, in which the office withdraws an override whose named server has got inside.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Never more than one server is inside the seat ledger, and whoever is inside is there legitimately -- the set of servers inside the ledger is a subset of the servers that are either named by a standing override or backed by a strict majority of the registrars.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: An administrative override is always honoured -- whenever the registrar's office names a server, that server eventually gets inside the seat ledger, no matter who is inside when the override is asserted and no matter whether the named server has any edit budget left.

---- MODULE W4Od13m8p0t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Technicians, Regions, Machines, NoTech, NoMachine

ASSUME NoTech \notin Technicians
ASSUME NoMachine \notin Machines

VARIABLES region, machine, homed, inNetwork, inBay

vars == <<region, machine, homed, inNetwork, inBay>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ region \in [Regions -> Technicians \cup {NoTech}]
    /\ machine \in [Machines -> Technicians \cup {NoTech}]
    /\ homed \in [Machines -> Regions]
    /\ inNetwork \in SUBSET Machines
    /\ inBay \in [Technicians -> Machines \cup {NoMachine}]

Init ==
    /\ region = [r \in Regions |-> NoTech]
    /\ machine = [m \in Machines |-> NoTech]
    /\ homed = [m \in Machines |-> CHOOSE r \in Regions : TRUE]
    /\ inNetwork = {}
    /\ inBay = [t \in Technicians |-> NoMachine]

\* A technician is compliant if it is out of every bay, or holds both
\* levels of the hierarchy for the bay it is standing in.
Compliant ==
    {t \in Technicians :
        \/ inBay[t] = NoMachine
        \/ /\ machine[inBay[t]] = t
           /\ region[homed[inBay[t]]] = t}

TakeRegion(t, r) ==
    /\ region[r] = NoTech
    /\ region' = [region EXCEPT ![r] = t]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<machine, homed, inNetwork, inBay>>

\* The fine lock is only reachable through the coarse lock above it.
TakeMachine(t, m) ==
    /\ m \in inNetwork
    /\ machine[m] = NoTech
    /\ region[homed[m]] = t
    /\ machine' = [machine EXCEPT ![m] = t]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<region, homed, inNetwork, inBay>>

OpenBay(t, m) ==
    /\ machine[m] = t
    /\ inBay[t] = NoMachine
    /\ inBay' = [inBay EXCEPT ![t] = m]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<region, machine, homed, inNetwork>>

CloseBay(t) ==
    /\ inBay[t] # NoMachine
    /\ inBay' = [inBay EXCEPT ![t] = NoMachine]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<region, machine, homed, inNetwork>>

\* Locks come off in the reverse of the order they went on.
DropMachine(t, m) ==
    /\ machine[m] = t
    /\ inBay[t] # m
    /\ machine' = [machine EXCEPT ![m] = NoTech]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<region, homed, inNetwork, inBay>>

DropRegion(t, r) ==
    /\ region[r] = t
    /\ \A m \in Machines : homed[m] = r => machine[m] # t
    /\ region' = [region EXCEPT ![r] = NoTech]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<machine, homed, inNetwork, inBay>>

\* The fleet changes size and shape underneath the crew, but only ever
\* through machines nobody holds.
Commission(m, r) ==
    /\ m \notin inNetwork
    /\ machine[m] = NoTech
    /\ inNetwork' = inNetwork \cup {m}
    /\ homed' = [homed EXCEPT ![m] = r]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<region, machine, inBay>>

Decommission(m) ==
    /\ m \in inNetwork
    /\ machine[m] = NoTech
    /\ inNetwork' = inNetwork \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<region, machine, homed, inBay>>

Next ==
    \/ \E t \in Technicians, r \in Regions : TakeRegion(t, r)
    \/ \E t \in Technicians, m \in Machines : TakeMachine(t, m)
    \/ \E t \in Technicians, m \in Machines : OpenBay(t, m)
    \/ \E t \in Technicians : CloseBay(t)
    \/ \E t \in Technicians, m \in Machines : DropMachine(t, m)
    \/ \E t \in Technicians, r \in Regions : DropRegion(t, r)
    \/ \E m \in Machines, r \in Regions : Commission(m, r)
    \/ \E m \in Machines : Decommission(m)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Whoever is in a bay holds the whole chain down to it, so no bay is ever
\* open to two technicians at once.
BaysAreHeldThroughTheHierarchy ==
    /\ Technicians \subseteq Compliant
    /\ \A t1, t2 \in Technicians :
         (inBay[t1] # NoMachine /\ inBay[t1] = inBay[t2]) => t1 = t2

====
nl:
An operator runs a network of vending machines across several service regions, maintained by a small crew of field technicians. The critical resource is a machine's restock bay: once a technician is inside a bay, the machine's cash box and product columns are open, and a second technician working the same bay at the same time means cash reconciles against the wrong shift and stock counts go wrong.

Access is arranged as a two-level lock. The coarse level is the region: a technician takes the region out of service, and only one technician can hold a region at a time. The fine level is the machine: within a region the technician holds is a set of machines, and taking a machine's lock requires already holding the lock on the region that machine is currently homed to. Only with the machine lock in hand can the technician open the bay. The two levels are always released in the reverse order: a technician cannot give a region back while it still holds a machine lock inside that region, and cannot give a machine lock back while it is still standing in that machine's bay.

The fleet is not fixed. Machines are commissioned into the network and decommissioned out of it while the crew is working, and a machine being commissioned is homed to whichever region the operator assigns it to, which need not be the region it was in before. Both of these are only allowed on a machine whose lock nobody holds, so the fleet can grow, shrink and be re-homed underneath the crew without ever pulling a region out from under a technician who is standing in one of its bays.

The full set of actions is: TakeRegion, in which a technician takes an unheld region; TakeMachine, in which a technician holding the region a commissioned machine is homed to takes that machine's unheld lock; OpenBay, in which a technician not already in a bay steps into the bay of a machine whose lock it holds; CloseBay, in which a technician steps out of the bay it is in; DropMachine, in which a technician gives back a machine lock it holds, provided it is not standing in that machine's bay; DropRegion, in which a technician gives back a region it holds, provided it holds no machine lock homed to that region; Commission, in which an unheld machine that is out of the network is brought into it and homed to a region; and Decommission, in which an unheld machine that is in the network is taken out of it.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every technician standing in a bay holds both levels of the hierarchy for that bay -- the machine's own lock and the lock on the region that machine is currently homed to -- and consequently no two technicians are ever inside the same machine's bay at once.

---- MODULE W4Od6m4p4t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Cars, Floors, QueueBound, NoFloor

ASSUME NoFloor \notin Floors
ASSUME QueueBound \in Nat \ {0}

VARIABLES pool, queue, running, panel

vars == <<pool, queue, running, panel>>

Drop(sq, f) == SelectSeq(sq, LAMBDA x : x # f)

Entries(c) == {queue[c][i] : i \in DOMAIN queue[c]}
Queued == UNION {Entries(c) : c \in Cars}
Running == {running[c] : c \in Cars} \ {NoFloor}
InSystem == pool \cup Queued \cup Running

TypeOK ==
    /\ pool \in SUBSET Floors
    /\ queue \in [Cars -> Seq(Floors)]
    /\ running \in [Cars -> Floors \cup {NoFloor}]
    /\ panel \in Floors \cup {NoFloor}

Init ==
    /\ pool = {}
    /\ queue = [c \in Cars |-> << >>]
    /\ running = [c \in Cars |-> NoFloor]
    /\ panel = NoFloor

Call(f) ==
    /\ f \notin InSystem
    /\ pool' = pool \cup {f}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, running, panel>>

\* Backpressure: a full queue simply is not offered the call, which stays
\* in the pool. There is no other way into a car's queue.
Assign(c, f) ==
    /\ f \in pool
    /\ Len(queue[c]) < QueueBound
    /\ queue' = [queue EXCEPT ![c] = Append(@, f)]
    /\ pool' = pool \ {f}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<running, panel>>

Dispatch(c) ==
    /\ running[c] = NoFloor
    /\ Len(queue[c]) > 0
    /\ running' = [running EXCEPT ![c] = Head(queue[c])]
    /\ queue' = [queue EXCEPT ![c] = Tail(@)]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, panel>>

Arrive(c) ==
    /\ running[c] # NoFloor
    /\ running' = [running EXCEPT ![c] = NoFloor]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, queue, panel>>

Designate(f) ==
    /\ panel = NoFloor
    /\ panel' = f
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, queue, running>>

\* The fire panel bypasses the queues entirely; whatever the car was
\* running goes back to the pool rather than into a queue, so no bound moves.
Preempt(c) ==
    /\ panel # NoFloor
    /\ panel \notin Running
    /\ running' = [running EXCEPT ![c] = panel]
    /\ queue' = [k \in Cars |-> Drop(queue[k], panel)]
    /\ pool' = (pool \cup {running[c]}) \ {NoFloor, panel}
    /\ UNCHANGED panel

Reset ==
    /\ panel # NoFloor
    /\ panel \in Running
    /\ panel' = NoFloor
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, queue, running>>

Next ==
    \/ \E f \in Floors : Call(f)
    \/ \E c \in Cars, f \in Floors : Assign(c, f)
    \/ \E c \in Cars : Dispatch(c)
    \/ \E c \in Cars : Arrive(c)
    \/ \E f \in Floors : Designate(f)
    \/ \E c \in Cars : Preempt(c)
    \/ Reset

Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(\E c \in Cars : Preempt(c))

\* The bound is a real bound on accepted work: no queue is over it, and no
\* call is counted both in the pool and in a queue.
CapacityIsRespected ==
    /\ \A c \in Cars : Len(queue[c]) <= QueueBound
    /\ pool \cap Queued = {}

DesignationsAreRun ==
    \A f \in Floors : (panel = f) ~> (f \in Running)

====

CONSTANTS
    Cars = {carA, carB}
    Floors = {flr1, flr2, flr3}
    QueueBound = 2
    NoFloor = nofloor

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT CapacityIsRespected

PROPERTY DesignationsAreRun
nl:
A skyscraper's elevator bank dispatches hall calls to a small number of cars. A hall call is raised at a floor and sits in a pool of unassigned calls until the dispatcher hands it to a car. Each car has a work queue of calls it has accepted, and that queue is deliberately small: a car that has accepted more stops than it can plausibly run within its service window gives every passenger on it a bad ride, so the dispatcher will not hand a car a call once its queue is at its bound. That refusal is the backpressure -- the call simply stays in the unassigned pool until some car has room, and there is no path that pushes work into a full queue.

A car takes calls off the front of its own queue one at a time. It can only pick up the next call once it has finished the one it is running, and finishing a call means arriving at that floor and letting the call go. A hall call is in exactly one place at any moment: unassigned, sitting in one car's queue, or being run by one car.

The building also has a privileged path: the fire panel. The fire service can designate a floor, and that designation does not join a queue and is not subject to backpressure at all. A designated floor is taken directly by a car, which drops whatever call it was running back into the unassigned pool to do it, and the designated floor is struck out of every car's queue at the same moment so it does not remain queued behind the car that is already running it. Only one designation can stand at a time, and the panel cannot be reset until some car is actually running the designated floor, so a designation cannot be quietly dropped.

The full set of actions is: Call, in which a floor that is nowhere in the system raises a hall call into the unassigned pool; Assign, in which the dispatcher moves an unassigned call onto the back of a car's queue, allowed only while that queue is below its bound; Dispatch, in which a car with an empty running slot takes the call at the front of its queue and starts running it; Arrive, in which a car finishes the call it is running and empties its running slot; Designate, in which the fire panel designates a floor while no designation stands; Preempt, in which a car takes the designated floor directly into its running slot, strikes that floor out of every car's queue so it is not left queued as well, and returns whatever it was running to the unassigned pool, allowed only while no car is already running that floor; and Reset, in which the fire panel clears a designation that some car is now running.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No car's queue ever exceeds its configured bound, and no hall call is ever both sitting in the unassigned pool and queued at a car, so the bound really is a bound on outstanding accepted work and cannot be evaded by double-counting a call.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every fire-panel designation is eventually run -- once the panel designates a floor, some car eventually has that floor in its running slot, regardless of how full the car queues are and regardless of what that car was running at the time.

CONSTANTS Controls, Feeders, Slots, MaxTerm, NoControl, NoSlot, NoFeeder

ASSUME NoControl \notin Controls
ASSUME NoSlot \notin Slots
ASSUME NoFeeder \notin Feeders

VARIABLES term, leader, heard, claim, book

vars == <<term, leader, heard, claim, book>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ term \in 0 .. MaxTerm
    /\ leader \in Controls \cup {NoControl}
    /\ heard \in [Controls -> 0 .. MaxTerm]
    /\ claim \in [Feeders -> Slots \cup {NoSlot}]
    /\ book \in [Slots -> Feeders \cup {NoFeeder}]

Init ==
    /\ term = 0
    /\ leader = NoControl
    /\ heard = [c \in Controls |-> 0]
    /\ claim = [f \in Feeders |-> NoSlot]
    /\ book = [s \in Slots |-> NoFeeder]

\* A node may only act as leader while the term it has heard of is current;
\* a slow node is still alive and still tries, and this is what stops it.
Current(c) == leader = c /\ heard[c] = term

Claimants == {f \in Feeders : claim[f] \in Slots}
Uncontested == {f \in Feeders : claim[f] \in Slots /\ book[claim[f]] \in {f, NoFeeder}}

StartTerm(c) ==
    /\ term < MaxTerm
    /\ term' = term + 1
    /\ leader' = c
    /\ heard' = [heard EXCEPT ![c] = term + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<claim, book>>

Learn(c) ==
    /\ heard[c] < term
    /\ heard' = [heard EXCEPT ![c] = term]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, claim, book>>

\* The promise and the booking are separate steps, so a promise can be
\* outstanding; no slot is ever promised to two feeders.
Promise(c, f, s) ==
    /\ Current(c)
    /\ claim[f] = NoSlot
    /\ book[s] = NoFeeder
    /\ \A g \in Feeders : claim[g] # s
    /\ claim' = [claim EXCEPT ![f] = s]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, heard, book>>

Book(c, f) ==
    /\ Current(c)
    /\ claim[f] \in Slots
    /\ book[claim[f]] = NoFeeder
    /\ book' = [book EXCEPT ![claim[f]] = f]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, heard, claim>>

\* Failover leaves promises that were never booked; the new leader clears them.
Cancel(c, f) ==
    /\ Current(c)
    /\ claim[f] \in Slots
    /\ book[claim[f]] = NoFeeder
    /\ claim' = [claim EXCEPT ![f] = NoSlot]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, heard, book>>

Release(c, f) ==
    /\ Current(c)
    /\ claim[f] \in Slots
    /\ book[claim[f]] = f
    /\ book' = [book EXCEPT ![claim[f]] = NoFeeder]
    /\ claim' = [claim EXCEPT ![f] = NoSlot]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, heard>>

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Controls : StartTerm(c)
    \/ \E c \in Controls : Learn(c)
    \/ \E c \in Controls, f \in Feeders, s \in Slots : Promise(c, f, s)
    \/ \E c \in Controls, f \in Feeders : Book(c, f)
    \/ \E c \in Controls, f \in Feeders : Cancel(c, f)
    \/ \E c \in Controls, f \in Feeders : Release(c, f)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Every feeder holding a claim finds its slot booked to itself or still
\* unbooked -- never booked to somebody else.
NoSlotAllocatedTwice == Claimants \subseteq Uncontested

====
nl:
A regional power grid runs a load shedder that puts feeders into rotating outage slots. There is one slot book for the whole region and a slot in it is a physical rotation window: putting two feeders into the same window sheds twice the load that was planned for it and can collapse the very thing the shedding was meant to protect.

Only one control node acts as the shedding leader at a time. Leadership is carried by a term number: starting a new term raises the term and installs whoever started it as leader, and every control node separately records the highest term it has heard about. A node only acts as leader while the term it has heard about is the current term. This is what handles a leader that is running slow: a node that has fallen behind is still there, still nominally the leader of an older term, and is perfectly capable of trying to act -- it is simply not allowed to, because the term it knows is no longer the current one. Nothing has to declare it dead and nothing has to time it out.

Placing a feeder is two steps rather than one, because the promise to a feeder and the booking of the slot are made by different parts of the system. The leader first promises a feeder a slot -- recording, against that feeder, the slot it will get -- and only afterwards books that slot in the region's slot book. Between those two steps the promise is outstanding: the feeder holds a claim on a slot the book has not yet written down. The leader will not promise a slot that any feeder already claims.

Failover leaves outstanding promises behind, so a leader for the current term can also cancel a promise that was never booked, and can release a feeder whose slot was booked, returning the slot to the book unbooked.

The full set of actions is: StartTerm, in which a control node raises the term, becomes leader, and records the new term as the one it knows; Learn, in which a node behind the current term catches up to it; Promise, in which the current leader gives an unplaced feeder a slot that is unbooked and that no feeder already claims; Book, in which the current leader writes into the slot book the booking for a feeder whose promised slot is still unbooked; Cancel, in which the current leader withdraws a promise that was never booked, leaving the feeder unplaced; and Release, in which the current leader takes a booked feeder back out, unbooking its slot and leaving the feeder unplaced.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A slot is never allocated twice -- every feeder that claims a slot finds that slot either booked to itself or not booked at all, and never booked to some other feeder, so no two feeders can end up sharing one rotation window.

ASSUME NoDrone \notin Drones
ASSUME MaxCapacity \in Nat \ {0}

Commands == [drone : Drones, stamp : 0 .. MaxEpoch]

VARIABLES epoch, credential, queue, capacity, running, runStamp

vars == <<epoch, credential, queue, capacity, running, runStamp>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ epoch \in 0 .. MaxEpoch
    /\ credential \in [Drones -> 0 .. MaxEpoch]
    /\ queue \in Seq(Commands)
    /\ capacity \in 1 .. MaxCapacity
    /\ running \in Drones \cup {NoDrone}
    /\ runStamp \in 0 .. MaxEpoch

Init ==
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ credential = [d \in Drones |-> 0]
    /\ queue = << >>
    /\ capacity = MaxCapacity
    /\ running = NoDrone
    /\ runStamp = 0

\* Authority only changes while the station is quiesced, so no command can
\* be left running across an epoch boundary.
ReKey ==
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ running = NoDrone
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<credential, queue, capacity, running, runStamp>>

Recredential(d) ==
    /\ credential[d] < epoch
    /\ credential' = [credential EXCEPT ![d] = epoch]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, queue, capacity, running, runStamp>>

\* Backpressure is the only gate on the queue, and only a current drone submits.
Submit(d) ==
    /\ credential[d] = epoch
    /\ Len(queue) < capacity
    /\ queue' = Append(queue, [drone |-> d, stamp |-> epoch])
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, credential, capacity, running, runStamp>>

\* Capacity moves at runtime but never below what is already accepted.
Resize(n) ==
    /\ n >= Len(queue)
    /\ n # capacity
    /\ capacity' = n
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, credential, queue, running, runStamp>>

Dispatch ==
    /\ running = NoDrone
    /\ Len(queue) > 0
    /\ Head(queue).stamp = epoch
    /\ running' = Head(queue).drone
    /\ runStamp' = Head(queue).stamp
    /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, credential, capacity>>

Discard ==
    /\ Len(queue) > 0
    /\ Head(queue).stamp # epoch
    /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, credential, capacity, running, runStamp>>

Complete ==
    /\ running # NoDrone
    /\ running' = NoDrone
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, credential, queue, capacity, runStamp>>

Next ==
    \/ ReKey
    \/ \E d \in Drones : Recredential(d)
    \/ \E d \in Drones : Submit(d)
    \/ \E n \in 1 .. MaxCapacity : Resize(n)
    \/ Dispatch
    \/ Discard
    \/ Complete

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(Complete)

\* Whatever is executing was stamped in the epoch that is still current, and
\* its submitter still holds a credential for that same epoch.
ExecutionIsCurrentlyAuthorised ==
    running \in Drones => (runStamp = epoch /\ credential[running] = epoch)

NothingInExecutionHangs ==
    \A d \in Drones : (running = d) ~> (running = NoDrone)

CONSTANTS
    Drones = {dr1, dr2}
    MaxEpoch = 2
    MaxCapacity = 2
    NoDrone = nodrone

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT ExecutionIsCurrentlyAuthorised

PROPERTY NothingInExecutionHangs
nl:
A wildfire surveillance swarm feeds observation commands from its drones into a single ground-station work queue, and the ground station executes them one at a time. The swarm is re-keyed periodically: a re-key raises the swarm's authorisation epoch, and every drone must separately pick up a fresh credential stamped with the new epoch before it counts as authorised again. A drone that has not picked up a fresh credential is stale -- it is still flying and still capable of submitting, it simply no longer speaks for the swarm.

Submissions go through backpressure. The queue has a capacity and a drone whose credential is current may only submit while the queue is below it; there is no other path into the queue. That capacity is not fixed. The ground station raises and lowers it at runtime as radio conditions change, but it will never lower it below the number of commands already sitting in the queue, so shrinking capacity throttles new work rather than silently dropping accepted work.

Every queued command carries the epoch it was submitted under. The ground station only ever executes a command from the front of the queue whose stamped epoch is the current one; a command at the front stamped with an older epoch is thrown away unexecuted rather than run. Re-keying is only allowed while the ground station has nothing in execution, so the swarm quiesces before its authority changes and no command can be left running across an epoch boundary.

The full set of actions is: ReKey, in which the swarm's authorisation epoch is raised while nothing is in execution; Recredential, in which a drone behind the current epoch picks up a fresh credential; Submit, in which a drone whose credential is current appends a command stamped with the current epoch to the queue, allowed only while the queue is below its capacity; Resize, in which the ground station sets a new capacity that is not below the number of commands already queued; Dispatch, in which the ground station, with nothing in execution, takes the command at the front of the queue into execution provided its stamp is the current epoch; Discard, in which the command at the front of the queue is thrown away unexecuted because its stamp is not the current epoch; and Complete, in which the ground station finishes whatever it has in execution.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The ground station never acts for a stale or unauthorised participant -- whenever a command is in execution, it was stamped with the epoch that is still current and the drone that submitted it still holds a credential for that same current epoch.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Nothing in execution ever hangs -- once the ground station takes a drone's command into execution, it eventually finishes it and returns to having nothing in execution.

VARIABLES status, claimant, journal, liquidity, token

vars == <<status, claimant, journal, liquidity, token>>

    /\ status \in [Instructions -> States]
    /\ claimant \in [Instructions -> Engines \cup {NoEngine}]
    /\ journal \in Seq(Instructions)
    /\ liquidity \in 0 .. PoolCeiling
    /\ token \in Engines

Init ==
    /\ status = [i \in Instructions |-> "queued"]
    /\ claimant = [i \in Instructions |-> NoEngine]
    /\ journal = << >>
    /\ liquidity = 0
    /\ token = CHOOSE e \in Engines : TRUE

Recorded == {journal[k] : k \in DOMAIN journal}
Settled == {i \in Instructions : status[i] = "settled"}

\* Only the token holder may take work out of the shared batch.
Claim(e, i) ==
    /\ token = e
    /\ status[i] = "queued"
    /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![i] = "claimed"]
    /\ claimant' = [claimant EXCEPT ![i] = e]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<journal, liquidity, token>>

Unclaim(e, i) ==
    /\ status[i] = "claimed"
    /\ claimant[i] = e
    /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![i] = "queued"]
    /\ claimant' = [claimant EXCEPT ![i] = NoEngine]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<journal, liquidity, token>>

\* The funds leaving, the status turning final and the journal entry are one
\* step; there is no path that does any of them without the others.
Settle(e, i) ==
    /\ status[i] = "claimed"
    /\ claimant[i] = e
    /\ liquidity >= Amount
    /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![i] = "settled"]
    /\ claimant' = [claimant EXCEPT ![i] = NoEngine]
    /\ liquidity' = liquidity - Amount
    /\ journal' = Append(journal, i)
    /\ UNCHANGED token

Fund ==
    /\ liquidity < PoolCeiling
    /\ liquidity' = liquidity + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<status, claimant, journal, token>>

PassToken ==
    /\ token' = CHOOSE f \in Engines : f # token
    /\ UNCHANGED <<status, claimant, journal, liquidity>>

Next ==
    \/ \E e \in Engines, i \in Instructions : Claim(e, i)
    \/ \E e \in Engines, i \in Instructions : Unclaim(e, i)
    \/ \E e \in Engines, i \in Instructions : Settle(e, i)
    \/ Fund
    \/ PassToken

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* settles unrecorded, and nothing is recorded that did not settle.
JournalMatchesSettlement == Recorded = Settled

CONSTANTS
    Engines = {corridorA, corridorB}
    Instructions = {pmt1, pmt2, pmt3}
    PoolCeiling = 2
    Amount = 1
    NoEngine = noengine

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT JournalMatchesSettlement
nl:
A clearing bank runs its end-of-day interbank settlement as a batch of payment instructions drawn against one liquidity pool at the central bank. Two settlement engines work the batch side by side. They were built by different teams for different corridors and share nothing except that one pool of central-bank liquidity and the batch itself.

Settling an instruction is irreversible: the funds leave, the counterparty is credited, and there is no unwind inside the batch. The permanent record of what happened is the settlement journal, an append-only list of instructions in the order they were settled. Everything else in the system is working state and can be rolled back; the journal cannot.

Access to the batch is arbitrated by a window token that passes around the engines in a ring. Only the engine holding the token may claim an instruction out of the queued state; once claimed, the instruction belongs to that engine and the engine can work it without the token. An engine may give a claim back, returning the instruction to queued for either engine to pick up later. Settling requires the engine to hold the claim and requires the liquidity pool to have the funds; the settlement takes the funds out of the pool, moves the instruction to settled, drops the claim, and appends the instruction to the journal in the same step. Nothing ever moves an instruction back out of settled, and nothing appends to the journal except a settlement.

The pool is topped up during the window from incoming receipts, which is what lets a batch settle more than the opening balance, and is the only thing that puts liquidity back.

The full set of actions is: Claim, in which the engine holding the token takes a queued instruction and becomes its claimant; Unclaim, in which an engine gives back an instruction it has claimed, returning it to queued; Settle, in which an engine settles an instruction it has claimed, provided the pool has the funds, deducting the funds, marking the instruction settled, dropping the claim and appending the instruction to the journal; Fund, in which a receipt tops the liquidity pool up by one, up to its ceiling; and PassToken, in which the window token moves to the other engine.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The settlement journal is exactly the set of settled instructions -- everything recorded in it is settled and everything settled is recorded in it -- so an instruction can neither be settled without appearing in the permanent record nor appear in that record more than once or without having been settled.

ASSUME NoMachine \notin Machines
ASSUME LeaseTerm \in Nat \ {0}

VARIABLES clock, holder, expiry, route, inside

vars == <<clock, holder, expiry, route, inside>>

Min(a, b) == IF a < b THEN a ELSE b

TypeOK ==
    /\ clock \in 0 .. WindowEnd
    /\ holder \in [Machines -> Planners \cup {NoPlanner}]
    /\ expiry \in [Machines -> 0 .. WindowEnd]
    /\ route \in SUBSET Machines
    /\ inside \in [Planners -> Machines \cup {NoMachine}]

Init ==
    /\ clock = 0
    /\ holder = [m \in Machines |-> NoPlanner]
    /\ expiry = [m \in Machines |-> 0]
    /\ route = Machines
    /\ inside = [p \in Planners |-> NoMachine]

Working == {p \in Planners : inside[p] \in Machines}
Covered ==
    {p \in Planners :
        /\ inside[p] \in Machines
        /\ inside[p] \in route
        /\ holder[inside[p]] = p
        /\ expiry[inside[p]] > clock}

Acquire(p, m) ==
    /\ clock < WindowEnd
    /\ m \in route
    /\ holder[m] = NoPlanner
    /\ holder' = [holder EXCEPT ![m] = p]
    /\ expiry' = [expiry EXCEPT ![m] = Min(clock + LeaseTerm, WindowEnd)]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, route, inside>>

Renew(p, m) ==
    /\ holder[m] = p
    /\ expiry[m] > clock
    /\ expiry' = [expiry EXCEPT ![m] = Min(clock + LeaseTerm, WindowEnd)]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, holder, route, inside>>

Handback(p, m) ==
    /\ holder[m] = p
    /\ inside[p] # m
    /\ holder' = [holder EXCEPT ![m] = NoPlanner]
    /\ expiry' = [expiry EXCEPT ![m] = 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, route, inside>>

Begin(p, m) ==
    /\ inside[p] = NoMachine
    /\ m \in route
    /\ holder[m] = p
    /\ expiry[m] > clock
    /\ inside' = [inside EXCEPT ![p] = m]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, holder, expiry, route>>

Finish(p) ==
    /\ inside[p] \in Machines
    /\ inside' = [inside EXCEPT ![p] = NoMachine]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, holder, expiry, route>>

\* The tick that runs a lease out is the tick that ends the work under it.
Tick ==
    /\ clock < WindowEnd
    /\ clock' = clock + 1
    /\ holder' = [m \in Machines |->

    /\ inside' = [p \in Planners |->
                    IF inside[p] \in Machines /\ expiry[inside[p]] <= clock + 1
                    THEN NoMachine ELSE inside[p]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<expiry, route>>

Add(m) ==
    /\ m \notin route
    /\ route' = route \cup {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, holder, expiry, inside>>

\* The route can shrink, but never out from under a lease.
Remove(m) ==
    /\ m \in route
    /\ holder[m] = NoPlanner
    /\ route' = route \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, holder, expiry, inside>>

    \/ \E p \in Planners, m \in Machines : Renew(p, m)
    \/ \E p \in Planners, m \in Machines : Handback(p, m)
    \/ \E p \in Planners, m \in Machines : Begin(p, m)
    \/ \E p \in Planners : Finish(p)

    \/ \E m \in Machines : Remove(m)

CONSTANTS

    Machines = {vmX, vmY}
    WindowEnd = 3
    LeaseTerm = 2
    NoPlanner = noplanner
    NoMachine = nomachine

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT WorkOnlyUnderALiveLease

PROPERTY LeasesDoNotOutlastTheWindow
nl:
A vending operator restocks its machines through route planners who take out short leases on individual machines. A lease names the machine, the planner who holds it, and the wall-clock time it runs out. Only the current leaseholder may open a machine and restock it, and the point of the expiry is that a planner who wanders off does not have to be detected or declared dead: the lease simply lapses and the machine becomes available again.

The service clock advances in ticks up to the end of the service window. A tick is also the moment leases are swept: every lease whose expiry time has been reached is torn down, and any restock in progress under such a lease is abandoned at the same instant. That is what makes the expiry real -- a planner cannot be left holding an open machine on a lease that has run out, because the tick that runs the lease out is the tick that ends the restock. A planner may renew a lease it still holds before it lapses, and may hand a lease back early provided it is not currently inside that machine. New leases cannot be taken out once the window has reached its end.

The route itself changes size while all this is going on: machines are added to the route and taken off it as sites open and close. A machine can only be taken off the route while nobody holds a lease on it, so the route can shrink underneath the planners without ever stranding one inside a machine that is no longer there.

The full set of actions is: Acquire, in which a planner takes an unleased machine that is on the route, before the window has ended, and gets a lease running to the lease term from now or the end of the window, whichever is sooner; Renew, in which a planner pushes out the expiry of a lease it still holds; Handback, in which a planner gives up a lease it holds on a machine it is not currently inside; Begin, in which a planner not already inside a machine opens one it holds an unexpired lease on and that is still on the route; Finish, in which a planner closes up the machine it is inside; Tick, in which the service clock advances by one, tearing down every lease that has reached its expiry and abandoning any restock running under one; Add, in which a machine is put on the route; and Remove, in which an unleased machine is taken off the route.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No planner ever acts under a stale or borrowed authority -- whenever a planner is inside a machine, that machine is on the route, its lease is held by that same planner, and that lease has not yet reached its expiry.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: No machine stays leased forever -- once a lease is taken out on a machine, that machine eventually becomes unleased again, whether the planner hands it back or the clock runs the lease out.

ASSUME NoSlot \notin Slots
ASSUME NoBox \notin Containers

VARIABLES blockLock, slotLock, homeOf, sitedAt, standingOn

vars == <<blockLock, slotLock, homeOf, sitedAt, standingOn>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ blockLock \in [Blocks -> Cranes \cup {NoCrane}]
    /\ slotLock \in [Slots -> Cranes \cup {NoCrane}]
    /\ homeOf \in [Slots -> Blocks]
    /\ sitedAt \in [Containers -> Slots \cup {NoSlot}]
    /\ standingOn \in [Slots -> Containers \cup {NoBox}]

Init ==
    /\ blockLock = [b \in Blocks |-> NoCrane]
    /\ slotLock = [s \in Slots |-> NoCrane]
    /\ homeOf = [s \in Slots |-> CHOOSE b \in Blocks : TRUE]
    /\ sitedAt = [c \in Containers |-> NoSlot]
    /\ standingOn = [s \in Slots |-> NoBox]

Sited == {c \in Containers : sitedAt[c] \in Slots}
Confirmed ==
    {c \in Containers : sitedAt[c] \in Slots /\ standingOn[sitedAt[c]] = c}
Occupied == {s \in Slots : standingOn[s] \in Containers}
Backed ==
    {s \in Slots : standingOn[s] \in Containers /\ sitedAt[standingOn[s]] = s}

TakeBlock(k, b) ==
    /\ blockLock[b] = NoCrane
    /\ blockLock' = [blockLock EXCEPT ![b] = k]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<slotLock, homeOf, sitedAt, standingOn>>

\* A slot lock is only reachable through the block the slot belongs to now.
TakeSlot(k, s) ==
    /\ slotLock[s] = NoCrane
    /\ blockLock[homeOf[s]] = k
    /\ slotLock' = [slotLock EXCEPT ![s] = k]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<blockLock, homeOf, sitedAt, standingOn>>

\* Both records are written in the one movement, which is what keeps them
\* inverse to each other.
Place(k, s, c) ==
    /\ slotLock[s] = k
    /\ standingOn[s] = NoBox
    /\ sitedAt[c] = NoSlot
    /\ sitedAt' = [sitedAt EXCEPT ![c] = s]
    /\ standingOn' = [standingOn EXCEPT ![s] = c]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<blockLock, slotLock, homeOf>>

Lift(k, s) ==
    /\ slotLock[s] = k
    /\ standingOn[s] \in Containers
    /\ sitedAt' = [sitedAt EXCEPT ![standingOn[s]] = NoSlot]
    /\ standingOn' = [standingOn EXCEPT ![s] = NoBox]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<blockLock, slotLock, homeOf>>

DropSlot(k, s) ==
    /\ slotLock[s] = k
    /\ slotLock' = [slotLock EXCEPT ![s] = NoCrane]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<blockLock, homeOf, sitedAt, standingOn>>

DropBlock(k, b) ==
    /\ blockLock[b] = k
    /\ \A s \in Slots : homeOf[s] = b => slotLock[s] # k
    /\ blockLock' = [blockLock EXCEPT ![b] = NoCrane]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<slotLock, homeOf, sitedAt, standingOn>>

\* Capacity is reshaped underneath the cranes, but only through idle slots.
Restripe(s, b) ==
    /\ slotLock[s] = NoCrane
    /\ standingOn[s] = NoBox
    /\ homeOf[s] # b
    /\ homeOf' = [homeOf EXCEPT ![s] = b]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<blockLock, slotLock, sitedAt, standingOn>>

Next ==
    \/ \E k \in Cranes, b \in Blocks : TakeBlock(k, b)
    \/ \E k \in Cranes, s \in Slots : TakeSlot(k, s)
    \/ \E k \in Cranes, s \in Slots, c \in Containers : Place(k, s, c)
    \/ \E k \in Cranes, s \in Slots : Lift(k, s)
    \/ \E k \in Cranes, s \in Slots : DropSlot(k, s)
    \/ \E k \in Cranes, b \in Blocks : DropBlock(k, b)
    \/ \E s \in Slots, b \in Blocks : Restripe(s, b)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* The plan and the ground are exact inverses, so no slot carries two bookings.
PlanAndGroundAreInverse ==
    /\ Sited \subseteq Confirmed
    /\ Occupied \subseteq Backed

====
nl:
A container terminal works its yard with gantry cranes. The yard is divided into blocks, each block is striped into ground slots, and every slot holds at most one box. Two boxes booked into the same ground slot is the failure being ruled out here: the second lift arrives to find the slot taken, the box goes down somewhere unrecorded, and the terminal loses it.

There are two records that have to agree. The yard plan records, for each container, the slot it is sited in. The ground record records, for each slot, the box standing on it. These are written by the same crane in the same movement, but they are separate records, and the terminal's whole idea of where anything is depends on them being exact inverses of one another.

Cranes coordinate through two levels of lock. The coarse level is the block: a crane takes a block before it can touch anything in it. The fine level is the individual slot, and a slot's lock can only be taken by a crane that already holds the lock on the block that slot currently belongs to. Only the holder of a slot's lock may put a box down on it or lift a box off it. Locks come off in the reverse order: a crane cannot give a block back while it still holds a slot lock inside that block.

The yard is re-striped while work goes on -- blocks are re-drawn and a slot can be moved from one block to another as the terminal reshapes capacity for a different ship. A slot can only be re-homed while nobody holds its lock and nothing is standing on it, so re-striping never moves a slot out from under a crane that is working it or a box that is sitting on it.

The full set of actions is: TakeBlock, in which a crane takes an unheld block; TakeSlot, in which a crane holding the block a slot currently belongs to takes that slot's unheld lock; Place, in which the crane holding a slot's lock puts a container that is not sited anywhere onto that empty slot, writing both the yard plan entry and the ground record in the one movement; Lift, in which the crane holding a slot's lock takes the box off it, clearing both records in the one movement; DropSlot, in which a crane gives back a slot lock it holds; DropBlock, in which a crane gives back a block it holds, provided it holds no slot lock inside that block; and Restripe, in which an unlocked, empty slot is moved into a different block.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The yard plan and the ground record are exact inverses of each other -- every container sited in a slot is the box the ground record shows standing on that slot, and every box standing on a slot is sited in that slot by the plan -- so no slot can ever be carrying two bookings.

EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Drones

Ballots == {"none", "yes", "no"}
Outcomes == {"open", "commit", "abort"}

VARIABLES fleet, sealed, ballot, decision, loaded, released

vars == <<fleet, sealed, ballot, decision, loaded, released>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ fleet \in SUBSET Drones
    /\ sealed \in SUBSET Drones
    /\ ballot \in [Drones -> Ballots]
    /\ decision \in Outcomes
    /\ loaded \in SUBSET Drones
    /\ released \in SUBSET Drones

Init ==
    /\ fleet = Drones
    /\ sealed = {}
    /\ ballot = [d \in Drones |-> "none"]
    /\ decision = "open"
    /\ loaded = Drones
    /\ released = {}

Authorised ==
    {d \in Drones : decision = "commit" /\ d \in sealed /\ ballot[d] = "yes"}

\* Fleet churn is independent of the transaction; it never touches the cohort.
Join(d) ==
    /\ d \notin fleet
    /\ fleet' = fleet \cup {d}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<sealed, ballot, decision, loaded, released>>

Leave(d) ==
    /\ d \in fleet
    /\ fleet' = fleet \ {d}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<sealed, ballot, decision, loaded, released>>

\* Sealing happens once and fixes who is party to this drop.
Prepare ==
    /\ sealed = {}
    /\ fleet # {}
    /\ sealed' = fleet
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fleet, ballot, decision, loaded, released>>

Vote(d, b) ==
    /\ d \in sealed
    /\ ballot[d] = "none"
    /\ decision = "open"
    /\ b # "none"
    /\ ballot' = [ballot EXCEPT ![d] = b]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fleet, sealed, decision, loaded, released>>

Commit ==
    /\ sealed # {}
    /\ decision = "open"
    /\ \A d \in sealed : ballot[d] = "yes"
    /\ decision' = "commit"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fleet, sealed, ballot, loaded, released>>

Abort ==
    /\ sealed # {}
    /\ decision = "open"
    /\ \E d \in sealed : ballot[d] = "no"
    /\ decision' = "abort"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fleet, sealed, ballot, loaded, released>>

\* The load leaves the bay for good; a drone with no load has nothing to drop.
Release(d) ==
    /\ decision = "commit"
    /\ d \in sealed
    /\ ballot[d] = "yes"
    /\ d \in loaded
    /\ loaded' = loaded \ {d}
    /\ released' = released \cup {d}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fleet, sealed, ballot, decision>>

Next ==
    \/ \E d \in Drones : Join(d)
    \/ \E d \in Drones : Leave(d)
    \/ Prepare
    \/ \E d \in Drones, b \in Ballots : Vote(d, b)
    \/ Commit
    \/ Abort
    \/ \E d \in Drones : Release(d)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(\E d \in Drones : Release(d))

\* Every drop was authorised by the commit it belongs to, and a drone that
\* has dropped is no longer carrying anything to drop again.
DropsAreAuthorisedAndSpent ==
    /\ released \subseteq Authorised
    /\ released \cap loaded = {}

CommitIsCarriedOutInFull ==
    (decision = "commit") ~> (sealed \subseteq released)

CONSTANTS
    Drones = {uav1, uav2, uav3}

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT DropsAreAuthorisedAndSpent

PROPERTY CommitIsCarriedOutInFull
nl:
A wildfire drone swarm carries out a coordinated retardant drop over a single ridge. Each drone carries exactly one load, and releasing it is irreversible: the load is gone, the ridge is covered, and a second release by the same drone is not a mistake that can be corrected -- there is nothing left to release. A partial drop is worse than none, so the swarm agrees the drop with a two-phase commit before anybody opens a hopper.

The live fleet changes while the swarm is airborne: drones come on station and go off station for fuel throughout the sortie, and that churn is not tied to the transaction. What the transaction runs against is a sealed cohort -- the snapshot of the fleet taken at the moment the drop is prepared. Sealing happens once. After it, drones joining or leaving the live fleet change nothing about who is party to this drop, and there is no second preparation.

Each drone in the sealed cohort votes once, yes or no. If every drone in the cohort has voted yes, the coordinator commits. If any drone in the cohort has voted no, the coordinator aborts. The decision is taken once and nothing takes it back: there is no path from committed to aborted or the other way round, because the drop it authorises cannot be undone.

Only after a commit does a drone open its hopper, and only a drone that is in the sealed cohort and voted yes may do so. Releasing moves the drone's load out of its bay for good; a drone with no load has nothing further to release.

The full set of actions is: Join, in which a drone comes on station and joins the live fleet; Leave, in which a drone goes off station and leaves the live fleet; Prepare, in which the coordinator seals the current live fleet as the cohort for this drop, provided nothing has been sealed yet and the fleet is not empty; Vote, in which a drone in the sealed cohort that has not yet voted casts a yes or a no, before any decision is taken; Commit, in which the coordinator decides to commit because every drone in the sealed cohort voted yes; Abort, in which the coordinator decides to abort because some drone in the sealed cohort voted no; and Release, in which a loaded drone of the sealed cohort that voted yes opens its hopper after a commit, moving its load out of its bay for good.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every drone that has released is one that was in the sealed cohort, voted yes, and released under a committed decision, and no drone that has released is still carrying a load -- so the irreversible drop happens only where it was authorised and never happens twice for the same drone.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: A commit is always carried out in full -- once the coordinator commits, every drone in the sealed cohort eventually releases its load, so the swarm never leaves the drop half done.

---- MODULE W4Od11m3p4t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Spoolers, PoolBound, MaxTerm, NoSpooler

ASSUME NoSpooler \notin Spoolers
ASSUME PoolBound \in Nat \ {0}

VARIABLES term, leader, heard, ledger, synced, inFlight

vars == <<term, leader, heard, ledger, synced, inFlight>>

RECURSIVE SumOver(_, _)
SumOver(f, S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET x == CHOOSE y \in S : TRUE
         IN f[x] + SumOver(f, S \ {x})

Committed == SumOver(inFlight, Spoolers)

TypeOK ==
    /\ term \in 0 .. MaxTerm
    /\ leader \in Spoolers \cup {NoSpooler}
    /\ heard \in [Spoolers -> 0 .. MaxTerm]
    /\ ledger \in [Spoolers -> 0 .. PoolBound]
    /\ synced \in [Spoolers -> 0 .. MaxTerm]
    /\ inFlight \in [Spoolers -> 0 .. PoolBound]

Init ==
    /\ term = 0
    /\ leader = NoSpooler
    /\ heard = [s \in Spoolers |-> 0]
    /\ ledger = [s \in Spoolers |-> 0]
    /\ synced = [s \in Spoolers |-> 0]
    /\ inFlight = [s \in Spoolers |-> 0]

Acting(n) == leader = n /\ heard[n] = term

TakeOver(n) ==
    /\ term < MaxTerm
    /\ term' = term + 1
    /\ leader' = n
    /\ heard' = [heard EXCEPT ![n] = term + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ledger, synced, inFlight>>

Learn(n) ==
    /\ heard[n] < term
    /\ heard' = [heard EXCEPT ![n] = term]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, ledger, synced, inFlight>>

\* A spooler that has just taken over is holding a ledger from another era;
\* reading the truth back in is what earns it the right to admit.
Resync(n) ==
    /\ Acting(n)
    /\ (synced[n] # term \/ ledger[n] # Committed)
    /\ ledger' = [ledger EXCEPT ![n] = Committed]
    /\ synced' = [synced EXCEPT ![n] = term]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, heard, inFlight>>

Admit(n, s) ==
    /\ Acting(n)
    /\ synced[n] = term
    /\ ledger[n] < PoolBound
    /\ ledger' = [ledger EXCEPT ![n] = @ + 1]
    /\ inFlight' = [inFlight EXCEPT ![s] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, heard, synced>>

\* Finishing does not touch anyone's ledger, so ledgers drift high, which
\* only ever makes the leader more conservative.
Finish(s) ==
    /\ inFlight[s] > 0
    /\ inFlight' = [inFlight EXCEPT ![s] = @ - 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, heard, ledger, synced>>

Next ==
    \/ \E n \in Spoolers : TakeOver(n)
    \/ \E n \in Spoolers : Learn(n)
    \/ \E n \in Spoolers : Resync(n)
    \/ \E n \in Spoolers, s \in Spoolers : Admit(n, s)
    \/ \E s \in Spoolers : Finish(s)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* The shared finishing pool is never oversubscribed, whatever leadership
\* did and however stale a ledger got.
PoolIsNeverOversubscribed == Committed <= PoolBound

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Spoolers = {siteA, siteB}
    PoolBound = 2
    MaxTerm = 2
    NoSpooler = nospooler

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT PoolIsNeverOversubscribed
nl:
A print shop runs two production sites that both draw from one shared finishing line. The finishing line can have only so many jobs in flight at once -- it is a physical pool of binding capacity, and pushing more than it holds jams it. The two sites are otherwise independent operations with their own presses, their own queues and their own operators; the finishing pool is the only thing they share, and neither can see the other's floor.

Because neither site can see the other, admission to the pool is not something either site decides for itself. One of the two spoolers acts as the admitting leader, and leadership is carried by a term number that goes up whenever a spooler takes over. Every spooler records the highest term it has heard of, and only a spooler whose recorded term is the current one is acting as leader.

The leader admits jobs against its own running count of how much of the pool is committed. That count is a belief, not the truth: it is the leader's own ledger, and a spooler that has just taken over is holding whatever ledger it happened to have from before, which may be wildly out of date. So a new leader must resynchronise before it admits anything -- it reads the true amount of work in flight across both sites into its ledger and records the term it did so in. Only a leader that has resynchronised in the current term may admit. A leader may also resynchronise again at any point where its ledger has drifted away from the truth, which is what lets it recover the capacity that finished work gave back. This is the whole safety argument for the shared pool: a leader admits against a ledger it knows is current, and increments that ledger as it admits, so it can never hand out more of the pool than the pool has.

Jobs finishing reduce the work in flight but do not touch anybody's ledger, so a leader's ledger drifts upward of the truth over time. That drift is in the safe direction -- it makes the leader more conservative, not less -- and resynchronising is what pulls it back.

The full set of actions is: TakeOver, in which a spooler raises the term, becomes leader, and records the new term as the one it has heard of; Learn, in which a spooler behind the current term catches up to it; Resync, in which the current leader, either because it has not resynchronised in this term or because its ledger no longer matches the truth, reads the true total work in flight into its ledger and records that it has resynchronised in the current term; Admit, in which the current leader, having resynchronised in this term and holding a ledger below the pool's bound, puts one more job in flight at one of the sites and raises its ledger by one; and Finish, in which a job in flight at a site completes and leaves the pool.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The total work in flight across both sites never exceeds the finishing pool's bound, however leadership changes hands and however stale a spooler's ledger has become.

---- MODULE W4Od4m1p6t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS RingSize, MaxCycle

ASSUME RingSize \in Nat \ {0}

Bays == 0 .. RingSize - 1

VARIABLES token, cycle, ticket, running, inService

vars == <<token, cycle, ticket, running, inService>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ token \in Bays
    /\ cycle \in 0 .. MaxCycle
    /\ ticket \in [Bays -> 0 .. MaxCycle]
    /\ running \in [Bays -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ inService \in SUBSET Bays

Init ==
    /\ token = 0
    /\ cycle = 0
    /\ ticket = [b \in Bays |-> 0]
    /\ running = [b \in Bays |-> FALSE]
    /\ inService = Bays

Firing == {b \in Bays : running[b]}
Cleared ==
    {b \in Bays : token = b /\ b \in inService /\ ticket[b] = cycle}

\* The token will not leave a bay that is still spraying.
PassToken ==
    /\ ~running[token]
    /\ token' = (token + 1) % RingSize
    /\ UNCHANGED <<cycle, ticket, running, inService>>

\* Recycling makes every ticket stale, so it waits for a quiet line.
Recycle ==
    /\ cycle < MaxCycle
    /\ \A b \in Bays : ~running[b]
    /\ cycle' = cycle + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, ticket, running, inService>>

Reissue(b) ==
    /\ ticket[b] < cycle
    /\ ticket' = [ticket EXCEPT ![b] = cycle]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, cycle, running, inService>>

Actuate(b) ==
    /\ token = b
    /\ b \in inService
    /\ ticket[b] = cycle
    /\ ~running[b]
    /\ running' = [running EXCEPT ![b] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, cycle, ticket, inService>>

Finish(b) ==
    /\ running[b]
    /\ running' = [running EXCEPT ![b] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, cycle, ticket, inService>>

TakeOffline(b) ==
    /\ b \in inService
    /\ ~running[b]
    /\ inService' = inService \ {b}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, cycle, ticket, running>>

BringOnline(b) ==
    /\ b \notin inService
    /\ inService' = inService \cup {b}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, cycle, ticket, running>>

Next ==
    \/ PassToken
    \/ Recycle
    \/ \E b \in Bays : Reissue(b)
    \/ \E b \in Bays : Actuate(b)
    \/ \E b \in Bays : Finish(b)
    \/ \E b \in Bays : TakeOffline(b)
    \/ \E b \in Bays : BringOnline(b)

\* Passing comes and goes as the holding bay sprays, so it needs strong
\* fairness; stopping a spray is always available, so weak fairness does.
Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ SF_vars(PassToken)
    /\ WF_vars(\E b \in Bays : Finish(b))

\* Anything spraying holds the token, is in service, and is on a current ticket.
OnlyClearedBaysFire == Firing \subseteq Cleared

TokenNeverComesToRest ==
    \A b \in Bays : (token = b) ~> (token # b)

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    RingSize = 3
    MaxCycle = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT OnlyClearedBaysFire

PROPERTY TokenNeverComesToRest
nl:
A car wash runs a conveyor line past a ring of treatment bays -- pre-soak, foam, rinse -- each with its own actuator. Only one bay may run its actuator at a time, and which one is decided by a control token that circulates the ring. The token visits every position on the ring in order, including positions whose bay is currently out of service; those simply pass it straight on.

The line runs in cycles. Each time the conveyor recycles, the cycle number goes up and every bay's authorisation ticket becomes stale. A bay must be reissued a ticket for the current cycle before it may actuate again: an actuator firing on a ticket from the previous cycle sprays the wrong chemical at the wrong car, and a bay that has simply not caught up is exactly the kind of participant that must not be allowed to act. The conveyor will not recycle while any actuator is running, and the token will not move on while the bay holding it is running, so nothing is ever left running under an authority that has moved on beneath it.

Bays go out of service and come back while the line runs -- a bay is taken offline for a blocked nozzle and brought back when it is cleared -- so the number of bays actually working the line changes as the line runs. A bay can only be taken out of service while its actuator is idle.

The full set of actions is: PassToken, in which the control token moves to the next position on the ring, allowed only while the bay currently holding it is not running its actuator; Recycle, in which the conveyor's cycle number goes up, allowed only while no actuator is running, which makes every bay's ticket stale; Reissue, in which a bay behind the current cycle is issued a ticket for it; Actuate, in which a bay that holds the token, is in service, and holds a ticket for the current cycle starts its actuator; Finish, in which a running actuator stops; TakeOffline, in which an in-service bay with an idle actuator is taken out of service; and BringOnline, in which an out-of-service bay is brought back.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every bay with a running actuator holds the control token, is in service, and holds a ticket for the cycle the line is currently in -- so no bay ever acts out of turn, out of service, or on stale authority.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: The control token never comes to rest -- whichever position holds it, it eventually moves off that position, so no bay can wedge the ring by holding the token and running its actuator forever.

---- MODULE W4Od5m5p5t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Players, Lobbies, NoLobby

ASSUME NoLobby \notin Lobbies

VARIABLES seat, ready, state, forced, roster, readyRoll

vars == <<seat, ready, state, forced, roster, readyRoll>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ seat \in [Players -> Lobbies \cup {NoLobby}]
    /\ ready \in [Players -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ state \in [Lobbies -> {"open", "launched"}]
    /\ forced \in SUBSET Lobbies
    /\ roster \in [Lobbies -> SUBSET Players]
    /\ readyRoll \in [Lobbies -> SUBSET Players]

Init ==
    /\ seat = [p \in Players |-> NoLobby]
    /\ ready = [p \in Players |-> FALSE]
    /\ state = [l \in Lobbies |-> "open"]
    /\ forced = {}
    /\ roster = [l \in Lobbies |-> {}]
    /\ readyRoll = [l \in Lobbies |-> {}]

Seated(l) == {p \in Players : seat[p] = l}
ReadyIn(l) == {p \in Players : seat[p] = l /\ ready[p]}

Launched == {l \in Lobbies : state[l] = "launched"}
Recorded == {l \in Lobbies : roster[l] # {}}
Entitled ==
    {l \in Lobbies :
        \/ l \in forced
        \/ 2 * Cardinality(readyRoll[l]) > Cardinality(roster[l])}

Sit(p, l) ==
    /\ seat[p] = NoLobby
    /\ seat' = [seat EXCEPT ![p] = l]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ready, state, forced, roster, readyRoll>>

Stand(p) ==
    /\ seat[p] # NoLobby
    /\ seat' = [seat EXCEPT ![p] = NoLobby]
    /\ ready' = [ready EXCEPT ![p] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<state, forced, roster, readyRoll>>

Ready(p) ==
    /\ seat[p] # NoLobby
    /\ ~ready[p]
    /\ ready' = [ready EXCEPT ![p] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<seat, state, forced, roster, readyRoll>>

Unready(p) ==
    /\ ready[p]
    /\ ready' = [ready EXCEPT ![p] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<seat, state, forced, roster, readyRoll>>

\* Force-starting is a decision about an open lobby; after launch it is
\* frozen along with everything else the record is judged on.
Force(l) ==
    /\ state[l] = "open"
    /\ l \notin forced
    /\ forced' = forced \cup {l}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<seat, ready, state, roster, readyRoll>>

Unforce(l) ==
    /\ state[l] = "open"
    /\ l \in forced
    /\ forced' = forced \ {l}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<seat, ready, state, roster, readyRoll>>

\* The one irreversible step: it freezes the roster and the ready roll.
Launch(l) ==
    /\ state[l] = "open"
    /\ Seated(l) # {}
    /\ \/ l \in forced
       \/ 2 * Cardinality(ReadyIn(l)) > Cardinality(Seated(l))
    /\ state' = [state EXCEPT ![l] = "launched"]
    /\ roster' = [roster EXCEPT ![l] = Seated(l)]
    /\ readyRoll' = [readyRoll EXCEPT ![l] = ReadyIn(l)]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<seat, ready, forced>>

Next ==
    \/ \E p \in Players, l \in Lobbies : Sit(p, l)
    \/ \E p \in Players : Stand(p)
    \/ \E p \in Players : Ready(p)
    \/ \E p \in Players : Unready(p)
    \/ \E l \in Lobbies : Force(l)
    \/ \E l \in Lobbies : Unforce(l)
    \/ \E l \in Lobbies : Launch(l)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* A record exists exactly for the lobbies that launched, and every record
\* shows a launch that was entitled to happen.
LaunchRecordsAreEntitled ==
    /\ Recorded = Launched
    /\ Launched \subseteq Entitled

====
nl:
A competitive game's matchmaker runs lobbies that players sit in before a ranked match. Launching a lobby is irreversible: the match is created on the ranked ladder, everyone on the roster has the result counted against their rating, and there is no un-launching it. A lobby launches at most once, and what it launched with is fixed at that instant.

A lobby launches on the strength of its own members. Each seated player may mark themselves ready or take that back, and a lobby may launch when a strict majority of the players seated in it are ready. There is also a moderator path: a moderator can force-start an open lobby, and a forced lobby may launch regardless of how few of its players are ready. Force-starting is a decision about an open lobby only -- a moderator can set it and take it back while the lobby is open, and once a lobby has launched neither is possible any more.

Launching freezes two things into the lobby's permanent record: the roster, meaning exactly the players seated in it at that instant, and the ready roll, meaning which of those players were marked ready. That record is what an appeal is judged against, and no later action touches it. A lobby that has not launched has no record at all.

The lobby itself carries on afterwards as a post-match room: players who were not on the roster can sit down in it and players can get up and leave, but none of that changes the roster or the ready roll that were frozen at launch.

The full set of actions is: Sit, in which an unseated player sits down in a lobby, whether that lobby has launched or not; Stand, in which a seated player gets up, clearing their ready mark; Ready, in which a seated player marks themselves ready; Unready, in which a seated player takes their ready mark back; Force, in which a moderator force-starts an open lobby; Unforce, in which a moderator takes a force-start back off an open lobby; and Launch, in which an open lobby with at least one player seated in it launches -- allowed only if it has been force-started or a strict majority of its seated players are marked ready -- freezing its roster and its ready roll into its record.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A lobby has a launch record exactly when it has launched, and every such record shows a launch that was entitled to happen: either the lobby was force-started, or a strict majority of the roster it launched with was on the ready roll.

---- MODULE W4Od19m0p5t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Patrons, Copies, MaxVersion, NoPatron

ASSUME NoPatron \notin Patrons
ASSUME MaxVersion \in Nat \ {0}

VARIABLES version, status, seenAt, issuedTo, collection

vars == <<version, status, seenAt, issuedTo, collection>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ version \in 0 .. MaxVersion
    /\ status \in [Patrons -> {"browsing", "attempting", "filled"}]
    /\ seenAt \in [Patrons -> 0 .. MaxVersion]
    /\ issuedTo \in [Copies -> Patrons \cup {NoPatron}]
    /\ collection \in SUBSET Copies

Init ==
    /\ version = 0
    /\ status = [p \in Patrons |-> "browsing"]
    /\ seenAt = [p \in Patrons |-> 0]
    /\ issuedTo = [c \in Copies |-> NoPatron]
    /\ collection = Copies

Filled == {p \in Patrons : status[p] = "filled"}
Named == {p \in Patrons : \E c \in Copies : issuedTo[c] = p}

Check(p) ==
    /\ status[p] = "browsing"
    /\ seenAt' = [seenAt EXCEPT ![p] = version]
    /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![p] = "attempting"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, issuedTo, collection>>

\* The compare-and-set: it only lands if nobody else's transfer moved the
\* register in between. Both records of the fill are written here together.
Transfer(p, c) ==
    /\ status[p] = "attempting"
    /\ seenAt[p] = version
    /\ version < MaxVersion
    /\ c \in collection
    /\ issuedTo[c] = NoPatron
    /\ issuedTo' = [issuedTo EXCEPT ![c] = p]
    /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![p] = "filled"]
    /\ version' = version + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<seenAt, collection>>

\* A patron only backs out when the register actually moved under it, or
\* when the register has run out of room to move at all.
Retry(p) ==
    /\ status[p] = "attempting"
    /\ (seenAt[p] # version \/ version = MaxVersion)
    /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![p] = "browsing"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, seenAt, issuedTo, collection>>

Acquire(c) ==
    /\ c \notin collection

CONSTANTS

    Copies = {copy1, copy2}
    MaxVersion = 2
    NoPatron = nopatron

PROPERTY SomeHoldIsEventuallyFilled
nl:
A public library runs reservations against a shared availability register. A patron with a hold checks what is available, and the register carries a version number that moves every time a copy is actually handed over. Handing a copy over is the irreversible step here: the hold is consumed, the copy is transferred out of the reservation system for good, and there is no path that gives a patron their hold back or takes a transferred copy back into the pool of things a hold can be filled from. A patron whose hold has been filled is finished and is not filled a second time.

Because several patrons check availability at the same time and any of them may be beaten to a copy, the register is not locked. A patron checks and remembers the version they checked at. When the transfer is attempted it is a compare-and-set: it only goes through if the register's version is still the one the patron checked at. If it is not -- because somebody else's transfer moved it -- the patron goes back to browsing and checks again. Backing out is only for that case: a patron whose remembered version is still current does not abandon its attempt, it waits for a copy, and it is only additionally allowed to back out once the register has reached its bound and can move no further.

The collection itself changes size while all of this is going on: copies are acquired into the collection and withdrawn from it as the branch rebalances its shelves. Acquiring is unrestricted, but the branch will not withdraw stock while any patron has an attempt in flight, so the shelves are never rebalanced out from under someone who is mid-transfer.

There are two records of a filled hold and they are written in the same step: the patron's own status turns to filled, and the copy's record names the patron it went to. The library's entire reconciliation depends on those two never disagreeing.

The full set of actions is: Check, in which a browsing patron reads the register's current version, remembers it, and moves to attempting; Transfer, in which an attempting patron whose remembered version still matches the register's version takes an unissued copy that is in the collection, marking that copy as issued to them and their own status as filled, and moving the register's version on by one; Retry, in which an attempting patron whose remembered version no longer matches the register, or whose register has reached its bound, goes back to browsing without changing anything; Acquire, in which a copy that is not in the collection is added to it; and Withdraw, in which a copy that is in the collection is taken out of it, allowed only while no patron has an attempt in flight.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The two records of a filled hold never disagree -- the set of patrons whose status is filled is exactly the set of patrons that some copy's record names -- so no hold is marked filled without a copy going out and no copy goes out without the hold it filled being marked.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: The optimistic scheme always eventually makes a transfer -- some patron's hold is eventually filled, however the collection is rebalanced and however many attempts are beaten and retried along the way.

CONSTANTS
    RingSize = 2
    MaxTally = 2
    MaxRevision = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec

nl:
A warehouse runs a fleet of picking robots that all report into one shared pick tally for a wave of orders. The tally is a single number -- how many items the wave has picked so far -- and it is the number the wave is closed against. The failure being ruled out is an update disappearing: a robot reads the tally, works out what it should become, and writes that number back; if the tally moved between the read and the write, writing back the number the robot worked out silently erases whatever moved it, and the wave closes short.

The tally carries a revision number that goes up every time it is written. A robot reads both together and remembers them. When it writes back, the write is only accepted if the revision it remembered is still the revision the tally carries -- otherwise the robot's reading is out of date and it has to read again before it can write.

The robots sit on a ring and a single work token circulates around the positions of that ring. Only the robot at the position currently holding the token may write the tally back, and only if it is actually part of the fleet at that moment. The token moves on unconditionally and visits every position on the ring, including positions whose robot is not currently in the fleet; those simply pass it on.

The fleet changes size while the wave runs. Robots are brought into the fleet as they come off charge and taken out of it as they go back on charge, and this happens without regard to where the token is. A robot outside the fleet keeps whatever reading it last took but cannot write anything back.

The full set of actions is: Read, in which a robot copies the current tally and the current revision into its own remembered reading; Write, in which the robot at the token position, if it is in the fleet, its remembered revision is still the current revision, and neither the tally nor the revision is at its ceiling, sets the tally to one more than the value it remembered and moves the revision on by one; PassToken, in which the work token moves to the next position on the ring; Enlist, in which a robot outside the fleet is brought into it; and Withdraw, in which a robot in the fleet is taken out of it.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No robot's reading can silently go stale under it -- every robot whose remembered revision is still the tally's current revision also holds exactly the tally's current value, so a write accepted by the revision check is always computed from the tally as it actually stands and can never erase another robot's write.
