CONSTANTS Shards, Slots, Players, NoPlayer

ASSUME NoPlayer \notin Players

VARIABLES votes, up, committed, loaded

vars == <<votes, up, committed, loaded>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ votes \in [Slots -> [Shards -> Players \cup {NoPlayer}]]
    /\ up \in SUBSET Shards
    /\ committed \in [Slots -> Players \cup {NoPlayer}]
    /\ loaded \in SUBSET Slots

Init ==
    /\ votes = [s \in Slots |-> [sh \in Shards |-> NoPlayer]]
    /\ up = Shards
    /\ committed = [s \in Slots |-> NoPlayer]
    /\ loaded = {}

Backers(s, p) == {sh \in Shards : votes[s][sh] = p}

\* The majority is counted over every shard there is, not over the ones
\* that are answering, so a silent failure can only ever withhold a win.
Winners(s) ==
    {p \in Players : 2 * Cardinality(Backers(s, p)) > Cardinality(Shards)}

Placed == {committed[s] : s \in Slots} \ {NoPlayer}
Settled == {s \in Slots : committed[s] \in Players}
Sound == {s \in Slots : committed[s] \in Players /\ Winners(s) = {committed[s]}}

Vote(s, sh, p) ==
    /\ sh \in up
    /\ committed[s] = NoPlayer
    /\ votes[s][sh] = NoPlayer
    /\ p \notin Placed
    /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![s][sh] = p]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<up, committed, loaded>>

Commit(s) ==
    /\ committed[s] = NoPlayer
    /\ Winners(s) # {}
    /\ committed' = [committed EXCEPT ![s] = CHOOSE p \in Winners(s) : TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, up, loaded>>

Load(s) ==
    /\ committed[s] \in Players
    /\ s \notin loaded
    /\ loaded' = loaded \cup {s}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, up, committed>>

\* Nothing announces this and nothing detects it.
Fail(sh) ==
    /\ sh \in up
    /\ up' = up \ {sh}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, committed, loaded>>

Return(sh) ==
    /\ sh \notin up
    /\ up' = up \cup {sh}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, committed, loaded>>

Next ==
    \/ \E s \in Slots, sh \in Shards, p \in Players : Vote(s, sh, p)
    \/ \E s \in Slots : Commit(s)
    \/ \E s \in Slots : Load(s)
    \/ \E sh \in Shards : Fail(sh)
    \/ \E sh \in Shards : Return(sh)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(\E s \in Slots : Commit(s))

\* A committed slot is committed to the sole player holding a majority for it.
SlotsAreSinglyWon == Settled \subseteq Sound

Won == {s \in Slots : Winners(s) # {}}

\* Voting is finite, so the won slots settle and stay settled.
WonSlotsGetCommitted == <>[](Won \subseteq Settled)

====
nl:
A game's matchmaker fills team slots for a ranked match. Each slot takes exactly one player, and a slot that ends up allocated to two players is the failure being ruled out: two clients both think they own the same position, both load in, and the match is unplayable.

There is no single authority that hands out slots. A set of matchmaking shards votes. Each shard may cast at most one vote per slot, naming the player it thinks should have that slot, and it can never take that vote back or change it. A slot is won by a player once a strict majority of all the shards -- counted over every shard there is, not over the ones that happen to be responding -- have named that player for it. Because every shard votes at most once per slot, two different players cannot both hold a majority for the same slot, and that is the entire argument that a slot is never allocated twice.

A shard can fail silently. It simply stops voting: nothing announces it, nothing detects it, and the rest of the system has no way to distinguish a shard that has crashed from one that is merely slow. Because the majority is counted against the full set of shards rather than the responding ones, a silent failure can only ever prevent a slot from being won, never cause it to be won by two players. A failed shard may come back later, and votes it cast before it failed still stand.

Once a slot has been won it is committed to its winner, and after that no further votes may be cast for it. A committed slot is then loaded into the match. A player already committed to some slot is not a candidate for any other, so votes naming an already-placed player are not cast.

The full set of actions is: Vote, in which a shard that is up and has not yet voted on an uncommitted slot names a player who is not already committed to another slot; Commit, in which an uncommitted slot that some player has a strict majority for is committed to that player; Load, in which a committed slot is loaded into the match; Fail, in which a shard that is up stops silently; and Return, in which a shard that has stopped comes back up with its earlier votes intact.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every committed slot is committed to the one player who holds a strict majority for it, and no other player holds a majority for that same slot -- so a slot is never allocated to two players at once.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Won slots do not sit unclaimed -- from some point on, every slot that some player holds a strict majority for is a slot that has been committed, and it stays that way however the shards fail and return.

TotalCoin == Cardinality(Machines) * StartingFloat

vars == <<routeLock, machineLock, hopper, bag, banked, onRoute>>

SumOver(f, S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET x == CHOOSE y \in S : TRUE
         IN f[x] + SumOver(f, S \ {x})

    /\ routeLock \in [Routes -> Collectors \cup {NoCollector}]
    /\ machineLock \in [Machines -> Collectors \cup {NoCollector}]
    /\ hopper \in [Machines -> 0 .. TotalCoin]
    /\ bag \in [Collectors -> 0 .. TotalCoin]
    /\ banked \in 0 .. TotalCoin
    /\ onRoute \in SUBSET Machines

Init ==
    /\ routeLock = [r \in Routes |-> NoCollector]
    /\ machineLock = [m \in Machines |-> NoCollector]
    /\ hopper = [m \in Machines |-> StartingFloat]
    /\ bag = [c \in Collectors |-> 0]
    /\ banked = 0
    /\ onRoute = Machines

TakeRoute(c, r) ==
    /\ routeLock[r] = NoCollector
    /\ routeLock' = [routeLock EXCEPT ![r] = c]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<machineLock, hopper, bag, banked, onRoute>>

\* The machine lock is only reachable through the route lock above it.
TakeMachine(c, m) ==
    /\ m \in onRoute
    /\ machineLock[m] = NoCollector
    /\ routeLock[RouteOf(m)] = c
    /\ machineLock' = [machineLock EXCEPT ![m] = c]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<routeLock, hopper, bag, banked, onRoute>>

Empty(c, m) ==
    /\ machineLock[m] = c
    /\ hopper[m] > 0
    /\ hopper' = [hopper EXCEPT ![m] = @ - 1]
    /\ bag' = [bag EXCEPT ![c] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<routeLock, machineLock, banked, onRoute>>

\* Coin goes back down as well as up; the float has to come from somewhere.
Float(c, m) ==
    /\ machineLock[m] = c
    /\ bag[c] > 0
    /\ bag' = [bag EXCEPT ![c] = @ - 1]
    /\ hopper' = [hopper EXCEPT ![m] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<routeLock, machineLock, banked, onRoute>>

Deposit(c) ==
    /\ bag[c] > 0
    /\ bag' = [bag EXCEPT ![c] = @ - 1]
    /\ banked' = banked + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<routeLock, machineLock, hopper, onRoute>>

DropMachine(c, m) ==
    /\ machineLock[m] = c
    /\ machineLock' = [machineLock EXCEPT ![m] = NoCollector]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<routeLock, hopper, bag, banked, onRoute>>

DropRoute(c, r) ==
    /\ routeLock[r] = c
    /\ \A m \in Machines : RouteOf(m) = r => machineLock[m] # c
    /\ routeLock' = [routeLock EXCEPT ![r] = NoCollector]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<machineLock, hopper, bag, banked, onRoute>>

Commission(m) ==
    /\ m \notin onRoute
    /\ onRoute' = onRoute \cup {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<routeLock, machineLock, hopper, bag, banked>>

\* No coin leaves the books by a machine leaving the network.
Decommission(m) ==
    /\ m \in onRoute
    /\ machineLock[m] = NoCollector
    /\ hopper[m] = 0
    /\ onRoute' = onRoute \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<routeLock, machineLock, hopper, bag, banked>>

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Collectors, r \in Routes : TakeRoute(c, r)
    \/ \E c \in Collectors, m \in Machines : TakeMachine(c, m)
    \/ \E c \in Collectors, m \in Machines : Empty(c, m)
    \/ \E c \in Collectors, m \in Machines : Float(c, m)
    \/ \E c \in Collectors : Deposit(c)
    \/ \E c \in Collectors, m \in Machines : DropMachine(c, m)
    \/ \E c \in Collectors, r \in Routes : DropRoute(c, r)
    \/ \E m \in Machines : Commission(m)
    \/ \E m \in Machines : Decommission(m)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Hoppers, bags and the bank always add back up to the shift's float.
CoinIsConserved ==
    SumOver(hopper, Machines) + SumOver(bag, Collectors) + banked = TotalCoin

====
nl:
A vending operator's cash is physical coin, and the audit that matters at the end of a shift is that the coin adds up. The shift starts with every coin sitting as float inside the machines' hoppers. From then on every coin in the operation is in exactly one of three places at any moment: inside a machine's hopper, in a collector's bag, or already paid into the bank. Nothing mints coin and nothing swallows it; all the actions do is move a coin from one of those places to another.

Collectors work the network under a two-level lock. The coarse level is the route -- north or south -- and a collector takes a route before touching anything on it. The fine level is the individual machine: a collector may only take a machine's lock if it already holds the lock on the route that machine belongs to, and only the holder of a machine's lock may open its hopper. Locks come off in the reverse order, so a collector cannot give a route back while it still holds a machine lock on that route.

Coin moves in both directions. A collector empties a coin out of a hopper it has open into its own bag, and pays coin out of its bag into the bank. It can also go the other way and put a coin from its bag back into a machine it has open, which is how a machine gets its change float back.

The network changes shape while the collectors work: machines are put on route and taken off route as sites open and close. A machine can only be taken off route once nobody holds its lock and its hopper is empty, so no coin is ever taken off the books by a machine leaving the network.

The full set of actions is: TakeRoute, in which a collector takes an unheld route; TakeMachine, in which a collector holding the route a machine belongs to takes that on-route machine's unheld lock; Empty, in which the holder of a machine's lock moves one coin from that machine's hopper into its own bag; Float, in which the holder of a machine's lock moves one coin from its own bag into that machine's hopper; Deposit, in which a collector pays one coin from its bag into the bank; DropMachine, in which a collector gives back a machine lock it holds; DropRoute, in which a collector gives back a route it holds, provided it holds no machine lock on that route; Commission, in which a machine is put on route; and Decommission, in which an unlocked machine with an empty hopper is taken off route.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Coin is conserved -- the coin in every machine's hopper, plus the coin in every collector's bag, plus the coin already banked, always adds up to exactly the float the machines started the shift with, no matter how the locks are taken, how the coin is moved, or how the network changes shape.

nl:
An airport's runway allocator hands out runways to approach controllers as leases. A lease names the runway, the controller holding it, and the allocation generation it was cut in. The allocator works in generations: it winds the current generation up, hands out leases against it, and when it starts a new generation every lease cut in an older one is dead.

A controller can fail silently. Its position goes dark with no alarm, no handover and no way for the allocator to tell it apart from a controller that is simply quiet. Nothing in the system detects the failure. What recovers the runway is the generation, not a detector: a lease cut in a superseded generation can be reaped by anyone, and the runway goes back into the pool. A controller that has gone dark may also come back up later.

Issuing a clearance onto a runway is the act that must never be done on stale authority. A controller may only issue one if it is up, holds the lease on that runway, that lease was cut in the generation currently running, and it has not already issued a clearance in this generation. A clearance already issued survives its controller going dark -- the aircraft is on the approach and the clearance stands -- so what the safety condition demands is that the clearance was authorised when it was issued and that the authority behind it has not been superseded since.

That is why the allocator will not wind the generation on while any clearance is still being worked: winding it on is precisely what would make a live clearance stale. The pattern has to empty first.

The full set of actions is: Grant, in which the allocator gives an unleased runway to a controller that is up, cutting the lease in the current generation; Advance, in which the allocator winds the generation on by one, allowed only while no clearance is being worked; Reap, in which a lease cut in a superseded generation is torn down and its runway returns to the pool; Clear, in which a controller that is up, holds a lease on a runway cut in the current generation, has no clearance of its own in progress and has not already cleared in this generation, issues a clearance onto that runway; Complete, in which a controller's clearance in progress finishes; Fail, in which a controller that is up goes dark silently; and Return, in which a controller that has gone dark comes back up.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No clearance ever rests on stale authority -- every controller with a clearance in progress holds the lease on the runway it cleared onto, and that lease was cut in the generation that is still running.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: The pattern always empties -- whenever there is a clearance in progress, there is eventually a moment with no clearance in progress at all, so the allocator can never be blocked forever from winding the generation on.

    /\ up \in SUBSET Controllers
    /\ manifest \in [Bins -> 0 .. MaxCount]
    /\ staged \in [Controllers -> Staging]

Init ==
    /\ term = 0
    /\ leader = NoController
    /\ up = Controllers
    /\ manifest = [b \in Bins |-> 0]
    /\ staged = [c \in Controllers |-> Clear]

Live == {c \in Controllers : staged[c].bin \in Bins /\ staged[c].era = term}
Grounded ==
    {c \in Controllers :
        /\ staged[c].bin \in Bins
        /\ staged[c].era = term
        /\ manifest[staged[c].bin] = staged[c].base}

\* Leadership and term move together, so no term ever has two leaders.
TakeOver(c) ==
    /\ c \in up
    /\ term < MaxTerm
    /\ term' = term + 1
    /\ leader' = c
    /\ UNCHANGED <<up, manifest, staged>>

Stage(c, b) ==
    /\ leader = c
    /\ c \in up
    /\ staged[c].bin = NoBin
    /\ staged' = [staged EXCEPT ![c] =
                    [bin |-> b, base |-> manifest[b], era |-> term]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, up, manifest>>

\* The compare-and-set, plus the term check that keeps a dangling update
\* from a controller that went dark out of the manifest.
Commit(c) ==
    /\ leader = c
    /\ c \in up
    /\ staged[c].bin \in Bins
    /\ staged[c].era = term
    /\ manifest[staged[c].bin] = staged[c].base
    /\ staged[c].base < MaxCount
    /\ manifest' = [manifest EXCEPT ![staged[c].bin] = @ + 1]
    /\ staged' = [staged EXCEPT ![c] = Clear]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, up>>

Abandon(c) ==
    /\ staged[c].bin \in Bins
    /\ staged[c].era # term
    /\ staged' = [staged EXCEPT ![c] = Clear]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, up, manifest>>

\* Nothing announces this and nothing rolls back what was in flight.
Fail(c) ==
    /\ c \in up
    /\ up' = up \ {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, manifest, staged>>

Return(c) ==
    /\ c \notin up
    /\ up' = up \cup {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, manifest, staged>>

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : TakeOver(c)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers, b \in Bins : Stage(c, b)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : Commit(c)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : Abandon(c)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : Fail(c)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : Return(c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Anything still committable was read from the count the manifest still shows.
NoUpdateCanBeLost == Live \subseteq Grounded

CONSTANTS
    Controllers = {ctlA, ctlB}
    Bins = {binL, binR}
    MaxCount = 1
    MaxTerm = 2
    NoController = noctl
    NoBin = nobin

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT NoUpdateCanBeLost
nl:
A warehouse keeps a shared pick manifest: for each bin, how many units have been picked out of it this wave. The manifest is updated by whichever robot controller is currently acting as the fleet leader, and the update is a read-modify-write -- read the bin's count, work out the new count, write it back. The failure being ruled out is the classic lost update: a write landing on a bin whose count has moved since it was read, silently erasing whatever moved it.

Leadership is carried by a term number. A controller takes over by winding the term up and installing itself, so leadership and term change together and there is never a term with two leaders. Every staged update records the term it was staged in.

A controller can fail silently. It stops, nothing announces it, and in particular a staged update it had in flight is simply left dangling: nobody rolls it back and nobody knows it is there. The recovery is not detection but the term. When another controller takes over, the term moves, and any staged update carrying an older term is no longer committable -- it can only be abandoned. This is the whole reason a dangling update from a controller that went dark can never land on a manifest that has moved on without it.

Committing is a compare-and-set: the leader may only write back if the bin's count is still the count its staged update was read from, and only if its staged update carries the current term. A controller has at most one staged update at a time.

The full set of actions is: TakeOver, in which a controller that is up winds the term on by one and becomes leader; Stage, in which the leader, being up and having nothing staged, reads a bin's current count and stages an update against it recording the current term; Commit, in which the leader, being up and holding a staged update carrying the current term whose recorded base still matches the bin's count, writes the count on by one and clears its staged update; Abandon, in which a controller drops a staged update whose term is no longer the current one; Fail, in which a controller that is up stops silently, leaving whatever it had staged exactly where it was; and Return, in which a controller that stopped comes back up.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No update can be lost -- every staged update that is still committable, meaning it carries the current term, was read from the bin count that the manifest still shows, so writing it back can only ever move that bin on from where it actually stands.

CONSTANTS Planners, Columns, Products, MaxStamp, NoOne, NoProduct

ASSUME NoOne \notin Planners
ASSUME NoProduct \notin Products

VARIABLES owner, stamp, worksheet, planogram, inService

vars == <<owner, stamp, worksheet, planogram, inService>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ owner \in [Columns -> Planners \cup {NoOne}]
    /\ stamp \in [Columns -> 0 .. MaxStamp]
    /\ worksheet \in [Planners -> SUBSET Columns]
    /\ planogram \in [Columns -> Products \cup {NoProduct}]
    /\ inService \in SUBSET Columns

Init ==
    /\ owner = [c \in Columns |-> NoOne]
    /\ stamp = [c \in Columns |-> 0]
    /\ worksheet = [p \in Planners |-> {}]
    /\ planogram = [c \in Columns |-> NoProduct]
    /\ inService = Columns

Written == UNION {worksheet[p] : p \in Planners}
Holders(c) == {p \in Planners : c \in worksheet[p]}
Unrecorded ==
    {c \in Columns : owner[c] # NoOne /\ c \notin worksheet[owner[c]]}

\* A planner will not touch another column while a grant it has been given
\* is still unwritten, so at most one column is ever out of step.
Take(p, c) ==
    /\ Unrecorded = {}
    /\ c \in inService
    /\ owner[c] = NoOne
    /\ stamp[c] < MaxStamp
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![c] = p]
    /\ stamp' = [stamp EXCEPT ![c] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<worksheet, planogram, inService>>

Record(p, c) ==
    /\ owner[c] = p
    /\ c \notin worksheet[p]
    /\ worksheet' = [worksheet EXCEPT ![p] = @ \cup {c}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, stamp, planogram, inService>>

Strike(p, c) ==
    /\ Unrecorded = {}
    /\ c \in worksheet[p]
    /\ worksheet' = [worksheet EXCEPT ![p] = @ \ {c}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, stamp, planogram, inService>>

\* The register is never handed back while somebody still has the column
\* written down as theirs; that ordering is the whole safety argument.
HandBack(p, c) ==
    /\ owner[c] = p
    /\ c \notin worksheet[p]
    /\ stamp[c] < MaxStamp
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![c] = NoOne]
    /\ stamp' = [stamp EXCEPT ![c] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<worksheet, planogram, inService>>

SetProduct(p, c, prod) ==
    /\ c \in worksheet[p]
    /\ planogram[c] # prod
    /\ planogram' = [planogram EXCEPT ![c] = prod]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, stamp, worksheet, inService>>

Install(c) ==
    /\ c \notin inService
    /\ inService' = inService \cup {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, stamp, worksheet, planogram>>

Retire(c) ==
    /\ c \in inService
    /\ owner[c] = NoOne
    /\ inService' = inService \ {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, stamp, worksheet, planogram>>

Next ==
    \/ \E p \in Planners, c \in Columns : Take(p, c)
    \/ \E p \in Planners, c \in Columns : Record(p, c)
    \/ \E p \in Planners, c \in Columns : Strike(p, c)
    \/ \E p \in Planners, c \in Columns : HandBack(p, c)
    \/ \E p \in Planners, c \in Columns, d \in Products \cup {NoProduct} : SetProduct(p, c, d)
    \/ \E c \in Columns : Install(c)
    \/ \E c \in Columns : Retire(c)

Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(\E p \in Planners, c \in Columns : Record(p, c))

\* Everything on a worksheet is in service and granted to exactly its writer.
NoColumnHeldTwice ==
    /\ Written \subseteq inService
    /\ \A c \in Columns : Holders(c) \subseteq {owner[c]}

\* A grant that the worksheets are behind on is always caught up on.
WorksheetsCatchUp == (Unrecorded # {}) ~> (Unrecorded = {})

====
nl:
A vending network is re-planogrammed by a team of planners working against the machines' column registers. Each product column has a register naming the planner that currently owns it, together with a stamp that moves every time the register changes. Taking a column is a compare-and-swap: a planner can only take a column whose register names nobody, and taking it names the planner and moves the stamp.

Owning the register is not the same as having the column on your own worksheet. A planner writes the column onto its own worksheet as a separate step after the register grants it, and the discipline that makes the whole thing safe is the order things come off in: a planner takes the column off its worksheet first, and only then hands the register back. The register is never released while somebody still has the column written down as theirs, which is what stops two planners ever having the same column on their worksheets at once.

A planner may set the product for a column that is on its worksheet, or clear it back to having no product set. Columns themselves come and go while the planners work: a machine is reconfigured and a column is installed or retired. A column can only be retired if its register names nobody, so retiring never takes a column away from a planner who is holding it; whatever product was set in it is still set if it is installed again.

The stamp on a register is bounded; once a column's stamp is at its ceiling the register can no longer be swapped either way. A planner will also not take a new column, or take one off its worksheet, while any column's register names a planner that has not yet written it down -- so at most one column is ever out of step between the registers and the worksheets.

The full set of actions is: Take, in which a planner, with no column currently out of step, compare-and-swaps an in-service column whose register names nobody and whose stamp is below its ceiling, naming itself and moving the stamp; Record, in which a planner writes onto its worksheet a column whose register already names it; Strike, in which a planner, with no column currently out of step, takes a column off its own worksheet; Hand back, in which a planner whose register names it for a column that is no longer on its worksheet swaps the register back to naming nobody and moves the stamp; SetProduct, in which a planner sets, changes or clears the product of a column that is on its worksheet; Install, in which a column is brought into service; and Retire, in which an in-service column whose register names nobody is taken out of service.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No column is ever allocated twice -- every column on anybody's worksheet is in service, and for each column the set of planners with it on their worksheet is contained in the single planner its register names, so two planners can never both hold the same column.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: The worksheets always catch up -- whenever some column's register names a planner that has not written it down, that gap is eventually closed and no column is out of step.

CONSTANTS RingSize, Slots, Orders, MaxSeq, NoOrder

ASSUME NoOrder \notin Orders
ASSUME RingSize \in Nat \ {0}

Desks == 0 .. RingSize - 1
Notices == [slot : Slots, order : Orders \cup {NoOrder}, seq : 1 .. MaxSeq]

VARIABLES token, booked, issued, believed, applied, inFlight

vars == <<token, booked, issued, believed, applied, inFlight>>

    /\ token \in Desks
    /\ booked \in [Slots -> Orders \cup {NoOrder}]
    /\ issued \in [Slots -> 0 .. MaxSeq]
    /\ believed \in [Slots -> Orders \cup {NoOrder}]
    /\ applied \in [Slots -> 0 .. MaxSeq]
    /\ inFlight \in SUBSET Notices

Init ==
    /\ token = 0
    /\ booked = [s \in Slots |-> NoOrder]
    /\ issued = [s \in Slots |-> 0]
    /\ believed = [s \in Slots |-> NoOrder]
    /\ applied = [s \in Slots |-> 0]
    /\ inFlight = {}

CaughtUp == {s \in Slots : applied[s] = issued[s]}
Agreeing == {s \in Slots : applied[s] = issued[s] /\ believed[s] = booked[s]}

Book(d, s, o) ==
    /\ token = d
    /\ booked[s] = NoOrder
    /\ \A t \in Slots : booked[t] # o
    /\ issued[s] < MaxSeq
    /\ booked' = [booked EXCEPT ![s] = o]
    /\ issued' = [issued EXCEPT ![s] = @ + 1]
    /\ inFlight' = inFlight \cup
         {[slot |-> s, order |-> o, seq |-> issued[s] + 1]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, believed, applied>>

Cancel(d, s) ==
    /\ token = d
    /\ booked[s] # NoOrder
    /\ issued[s] < MaxSeq
    /\ booked' = [booked EXCEPT ![s] = NoOrder]
    /\ issued' = [issued EXCEPT ![s] = @ + 1]
    /\ inFlight' = inFlight \cup
         {[slot |-> s, order |-> NoOrder, seq |-> issued[s] + 1]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, believed, applied>>

\* The sequence carried by the notice is the only thing that tells the site
\* how recent it is, because the link hands them over in any order at all.
Apply(m) ==
    /\ m \in inFlight
    /\ m.seq > applied[m.slot]
    /\ believed' = [believed EXCEPT ![m.slot] = m.order]
    /\ applied' = [applied EXCEPT ![m.slot] = m.seq]
    /\ inFlight' = inFlight \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, booked, issued>>

\* A notice describing a superseded state of the slot is thrown away.
Discard(m) ==
    /\ m \in inFlight
    /\ m.seq <= applied[m.slot]
    /\ inFlight' = inFlight \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, booked, issued, believed, applied>>

PassToken ==
    /\ token' = (token + 1) % RingSize
    /\ UNCHANGED <<booked, issued, believed, applied, inFlight>>

Next ==
    \/ \E d \in Desks, s \in Slots, o \in Orders : Book(d, s, o)
    \/ \E d \in Desks, s \in Slots : Cancel(d, s)
    \/ \E m \in Notices : Apply(m)
    \/ \E m \in Notices : Discard(m)
    \/ PassToken

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* The site is never ahead of the desks, and where it has caught up the
\* two books name the same holder for the slot.
BooksCannotDivergeUnderReordering ==
    /\ \A s \in Slots : applied[s] <= issued[s]
    /\ CaughtUp \subseteq Agreeing

CONSTANTS
    RingSize = 2
    Slots = {dockA, dockB}
    Orders = {ord1}
    MaxSeq = 2
    NoOrder = noorder

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT BooksCannotDivergeUnderReordering
nl:
A vending operator books restock deliveries into numbered dock slots at each site. Two dispatch desks share the booking book, and a work token circulates between them in a ring: only the desk holding the token may change a booking. The site itself does not hold the book -- it learns about bookings from notices the desks send it.

The link to the site reorders. Notices are not delivered in the order they were sent: a notice sent first can arrive after one sent later, and the site has no way to tell from the notice itself how recent it is other than by what the notice carries. That is why every notice carries the sequence number the desks stamped it with. The desks keep a per-slot sequence that goes up on every change they make, and the notice carries the number the change was made at.

The site keeps, per slot, the booking it currently believes and the highest sequence number it has applied. A notice is applied only if its sequence number is higher than the highest the site has applied for that slot; a notice whose number is not higher is dropped unapplied, because it is describing a state of the slot that has already been superseded. This is the entire defence against reordering: a stale notice arriving late cannot reinstate an old booking and leave the site believing a dock slot is held by an order that the desks have since moved elsewhere.

A desk will not book an order into a slot if that order is already booked into another slot, and will not book into a slot that is already booked.

The full set of actions is: Book, in which the desk holding the token books an unbooked order into an unbooked slot, moves that slot's sequence on by one and puts a notice carrying the new sequence into flight; Cancel, in which the desk holding the token clears a booked slot, moves that slot's sequence on by one and puts a notice carrying the new sequence into flight; Apply, in which a notice in flight whose sequence is higher than the highest the site has applied for that slot is applied, setting the site's belief about the slot and its highest applied sequence, and leaving flight; Discard, in which a notice in flight whose sequence is not higher than the highest applied for that slot leaves flight unapplied; and PassToken, in which the work token moves to the other desk.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A dock slot is never held by two different orders across the two books -- the site is never ahead of the desks on any slot's sequence, and any slot on which the site has caught up to the desks' sequence is a slot the site and the desks agree the owner of.

EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Boxes, LaneBound, NoBox

ASSUME NoBox \notin Boxes
ASSUME LaneBound \in Nat \ {0}

VARIABLES place, gate, designated, manifest, cleared

vars == <<place, gate, designated, manifest, cleared>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ place \in [Boxes -> {"yard", "lane", "gone"}]
    /\ gate \in Boxes \cup {NoBox}
    /\ designated \in Boxes \cup {NoBox}
    /\ manifest \in SUBSET Boxes
    /\ cleared \in SUBSET Boxes

Init ==
    /\ place = [b \in Boxes |-> "yard"]
    /\ gate = NoBox
    /\ designated = NoBox
    /\ manifest = {}
    /\ cleared = {}

InLane == {b \in Boxes : place[b] = "lane"}
Gone == {b \in Boxes : place[b] = "gone"}

Clear(b) ==
    /\ b \notin cleared
    /\ cleared' = cleared \cup {b}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<place, gate, designated, manifest>>

Revoke(b) ==
    /\ b \in cleared
    /\ cleared' = cleared \ {b}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<place, gate, designated, manifest>>

\* Backpressure: the bound is checked here and nowhere is it bypassed,
\* not even on the manager's path.
Stage(b) ==
    /\ place[b] = "yard"
    /\ Cardinality(InLane) < LaneBound
    /\ designated \in {NoBox, b}
    /\ \/ b \in cleared
       \/ designated = b
    /\ place' = [place EXCEPT ![b] = "lane"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<gate, designated, manifest, cleared>>

\* The designated box is never pulled back out of the lane.
Unstage(b) ==
    /\ place[b] = "lane"
    /\ gate # b
    /\ designated # b
    /\ place' = [place EXCEPT ![b] = "yard"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<gate, designated, manifest, cleared>>

ToGate(b) ==
    /\ place[b] = "lane"
    /\ gate = NoBox
    /\ designated \in {NoBox, b}
    /\ gate' = b
    /\ UNCHANGED <<place, designated, manifest, cleared>>

\* The one irreversible step: nothing brings a box back from here.
Discharge(b) ==
    /\ gate = b
    /\ place' = [place EXCEPT ![b] = "gone"]
    /\ manifest' = manifest \cup {b}
    /\ gate' = NoBox
    /\ UNCHANGED <<designated, cleared>>

Designate(b) ==
    /\ designated = NoBox
    /\ place[b] = "yard"
    /\ designated' = b
    /\ UNCHANGED <<place, gate, manifest, cleared>>

Lift(b) ==
    /\ designated = b
    /\ place[b] = "gone"
    /\ designated' = NoBox
    /\ UNCHANGED <<place, gate, manifest, cleared>>

Next ==
    \/ \E b \in Boxes : Clear(b)
    \/ \E b \in Boxes : Revoke(b)
    \/ \E b \in Boxes : Stage(b)
    \/ \E b \in Boxes : Unstage(b)
    \/ \E b \in Boxes : ToGate(b)
    \/ \E b \in Boxes : Discharge(b)
    \/ \E b \in Boxes : Designate(b)
    \/ \E b \in Boxes : Lift(b)

Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(\E b \in Boxes : Discharge(b))
    /\ WF_vars(\E b \in Boxes : Unstage(b))
    /\ WF_vars(\E b \in Boxes : Stage(b))
    /\ WF_vars(\E b \in Boxes : ToGate(b))

\* The manifest is exactly what has left, and the lane keeps to its bound.
DischargeIsFinalAndBounded ==
    /\ Gone = manifest
    /\ Cardinality(InLane) <= LaneBound

DesignationsAreDischarged ==
    \A b \in Boxes : (designated = b) ~> (place[b] = "gone")

CONSTANTS
    Boxes = {bx1, bx2, bx3}
    LaneBound = 1
    NoBox = nobox

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT DischargeIsFinalAndBounded

PROPERTY DesignationsAreDischarged
nl:
A container terminal discharges boxes out of the yard through a single gate lane. Discharging a box is irreversible: the box leaves the terminal's custody, goes onto the permanent discharge manifest, and there is no action anywhere that brings it back into the yard or takes it off the manifest. A box is discharged at most once because once it is gone it is no longer in the yard to be staged again.

The gate lane is a bounded work queue and the bound is the backpressure: a box can only be staged into the lane while the lane is below its bound, so a busy gate simply refuses new work and boxes wait in the yard. A staged box that is not currently at the gate and is not the manager's designated box can be pulled back to the yard to make room. From the lane a box moves to the gate itself, which handles one box at a time, and from the gate it is discharged.

Normally a box may only be staged once customs has cleared it, and customs can revoke a clearance again at any time. The terminal manager has a privileged path around this: the manager can designate one box -- a reefer running out of power, a box a ship is waiting on -- and a designated box may be staged whether or not customs has cleared it. While a designation is standing it also takes priority absolutely: no other box may be staged into the lane and no other box may be moved onto the gate, so the lane drains and the gate frees up in front of the designated box. The manager cannot lift a designation until the box it names has actually been discharged, and cannot designate a second box while one designation stands.

The full set of actions is: Clear, in which customs clears a box; Revoke, in which customs takes a clearance back off a box; Stage, in which a box in the yard that is either customs-cleared or the designated box moves into the lane, allowed only while the lane is below its bound and only if no other box is designated; Unstage, in which a box in the lane that is not at the gate and is not the designated box is pulled back to the yard; ToGate, in which a box in the lane moves onto the free gate, allowed only if no other box is designated; Discharge, in which the box at the gate leaves the terminal for good, going onto the permanent discharge manifest and freeing the gate; Designate, in which the manager designates a box in the yard while no designation stands; and Lift, in which the manager lifts a designation whose box has been discharged.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A box appears on the permanent discharge manifest exactly when it has left the terminal, and the gate lane never holds more boxes than its bound -- so no box is discharged twice or discharged without being recorded, and the backpressure on the lane is never evaded, not even by the manager's designated box.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: A designation is always carried out -- once the manager designates a box, that box is eventually discharged, however full the lane is when the designation is made and whether or not customs ever clears it.

    /\ heldVersion \in [Desks -> 0 .. MaxVersion]
    /\ editing \in [Desks -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ dayList \in [Sessions -> Theatres \cup {NoTheatre}]

    /\ cellVersion = 0
    /\ heldVersion = [d \in Desks |-> 0]
    /\ editing = [d \in Desks |-> FALSE]
    /\ dayList = [s \in Sessions |-> NoTheatre]

    /\ editing[d]
    /\ editing' = [editing EXCEPT ![d] = FALSE]

    /\ ~editing[d]
    /\ cellOwner' = NoDesk

    \/ Republish
    \/ \E d \in Desks : Refresh(d)
    \/ \E d \in Desks : OpenEdit(d)
    \/ \E d \in Desks, s \in Sessions, t \in Theatres \cup {NoTheatre} :

\* Anyone with an edit open owns the register and is on its current version.
EditsRestOnCurrentAuthority == Open \subseteq Entitled

nl:
A hospital's theatre scheduling desks all edit one day list -- which session runs in which theatre. Which desk may edit is decided by a single register cell holding two things: the desk that currently owns it, and a version number for the day plan the owner is working against. A desk takes the cell by swapping itself into it while it names nobody, and gives it back by swapping nobody in.

The day plan is republished from outside the desks -- a theatre goes down for a deep clean, an emergency list lands -- and republishing moves the register's version on. A desk that took the cell before a republication is still holding it, but the version it took the cell at is now behind the register's version. That desk is not broken and nothing needs to time it out: it is simply slow, it is still there, and when it comes back it must refresh its version against the register before it may touch the day list again. A desk that is behind and tries to edit anyway is exactly the stale participant this rules out.

Editing the day list happens in a bracket: the desk opens an edit, makes amendments while it is open, and closes it. The plan is never republished while any desk has an edit open, because doing so is precisely what would leave a live edit standing on a superseded plan.

The full set of actions is: Take, in which a desk swaps itself into a register cell that names nobody, adopting the register's current version as the version it holds; Republish, in which the day plan's version moves on by one, allowed only while no desk has an edit open; Refresh, in which the desk that owns the register and is behind the register's version catches up to it; Open, in which the owning desk, holding the register's current version and with no edit already open, opens an edit; Amend, in which a desk with an edit open moves a session into a theatre or out of one; Close, in which a desk closes its open edit; and Hand back, in which the owning desk, with no edit open, swaps nobody back into the register.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No desk ever edits on stale authority -- every desk with an edit open is the desk the register cell names and holds exactly the version the register currently carries.

---- MODULE W4Od2m0p6t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Robots, MaxEpoch, MaxVersion

ASSUME MaxVersion \in Nat \ {0}

Attempts == [live : BOOLEAN, at : 0 .. MaxVersion, era : 0 .. MaxEpoch]
Idle == [live |-> FALSE, at |-> 0, era |-> 0]

VARIABLES epoch, credential, version, attempt, up

vars == <<epoch, credential, version, attempt, up>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ epoch \in 0 .. MaxEpoch
    /\ credential \in [Robots -> 0 .. MaxEpoch]
    /\ version \in 0 .. MaxVersion
    /\ attempt \in [Robots -> Attempts]
    /\ up \in SUBSET Robots

Init ==
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ credential = [r \in Robots |-> 0]
    /\ version = 0
    /\ attempt = [r \in Robots |-> Idle]
    /\ up = Robots

InFlight == {r \in Robots : attempt[r].live}
Committable ==
    {r \in Robots :
        attempt[r].live /\ attempt[r].at = version /\ attempt[r].era = epoch}
Credentialed ==
    {r \in Robots :
        /\ attempt[r].live
        /\ attempt[r].at = version
        /\ attempt[r].era = epoch
        /\ credential[r] = epoch}

\* No attempt is ever half-run across an epoch boundary.
ReKey ==
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ InFlight = {}
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<credential, version, attempt, up>>

Recredential(r) ==
    /\ r \in up
    /\ credential[r] < epoch
    /\ credential' = [credential EXCEPT ![r] = epoch]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, version, attempt, up>>

Begin(r) ==
    /\ r \in up
    /\ credential[r] = epoch
    /\ ~attempt[r].live
    /\ attempt' = [attempt EXCEPT ![r] =
                     [live |-> TRUE, at |-> version, era |-> epoch]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, credential, version, up>>

\* The compare-and-set and the credential check, both at the last moment.
Commit(r) ==
    /\ r \in up
    /\ credential[r] = epoch
    /\ attempt[r].live
    /\ attempt[r].at = version
    /\ attempt[r].era = epoch
    /\ version < MaxVersion
    /\ version' = version + 1
    /\ attempt' = [attempt EXCEPT ![r] = Idle]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, credential, up>>

Abandon(r) ==
    /\ attempt[r].live
    /\ (attempt[r].at # version \/ attempt[r].era # epoch)
    /\ attempt' = [attempt EXCEPT ![r] = Idle]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, credential, version, up>>

\* Nothing announces this and nothing cleans up after it.
Fail(r) ==
    /\ r \in up
    /\ up' = up \ {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, credential, version, attempt>>

Return(r) ==
    /\ r \notin up
    /\ up' = up \cup {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, credential, version, attempt>>

Next ==
    \/ ReKey
    \/ \E r \in Robots : Recredential(r)
    \/ \E r \in Robots : Begin(r)
    \/ \E r \in Robots : Commit(r)
    \/ \E r \in Robots : Abandon(r)
    \/ \E r \in Robots : Fail(r)
    \/ \E r \in Robots : Return(r)

\* Returning and abandoning a dead attempt stay available once they are
\* possible, so weak fairness carries them; recredentialling, beginning and
\* committing all keep being cut off by silent failures, so they need
\* strong fairness to be guaranteed at all.
Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(\E r \in Robots : Return(r))
    /\ SF_vars(\E r \in Robots : Recredential(r))
    /\ WF_vars(\E r \in Robots : Abandon(r))
    /\ SF_vars(\E r \in Robots : Begin(r))
    /\ SF_vars(\E r \in Robots : Commit(r))

\* Anything still committable is held by a robot with a current credential.
CommittableWorkIsCredentialled == Committable \subseteq Credentialed

BoardAlwaysMakesProgress == <>(version = MaxVersion)

====

CONSTANTS
    Robots = {botA, botB}
    MaxEpoch = 1
    MaxVersion = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT CommittableWorkIsCredentialled

PROPERTY BoardAlwaysMakesProgress
nl:
A warehouse robot fleet writes to one shared task board. There is no lock on the board: a robot reads the board's version, works out its change, and commits with a compare-and-set that only lands if the version has not moved. If it has moved, the robot's attempt is dead and it abandons it and starts again.

Authority to write is separate from the optimism. The fleet is re-keyed periodically -- the shift changes, the site's key rotates -- and a re-key moves the fleet's authorisation epoch. A robot has to pick up a credential for the current epoch before it may start an attempt, and every attempt records the epoch it was started in. An attempt started in a superseded epoch is dead the same way a beaten compare-and-set is dead: it is abandoned, not committed. A re-key is only taken while no attempt is in flight, so no attempt is ever half-run across an epoch boundary.

A robot can fail silently: it stops, nothing announces it, and an attempt it had in flight simply stays in flight with nobody working it. There is no detector and no timeout. What makes that safe is that a dangling attempt is still subject to both checks when anybody looks at it: it is only committable while its recorded version is still the board's version and its recorded epoch is still the fleet's epoch, and the robot itself must still hold a credential for that epoch. A robot that stopped may come back later with its attempt and its credential as it left them.

The full set of actions is: ReKey, in which the fleet's authorisation epoch moves on by one, allowed only while no attempt is in flight; Recredential, in which a robot that is up and behind the current epoch picks up a credential for it; Begin, in which a robot that is up, holds a current credential and has no attempt in flight starts one, recording the board's current version and the current epoch; Commit, in which a robot that is up, holds a current credential and an attempt in flight whose recorded version and epoch are both still current, moves the board's version on by one and ends its attempt; Abandon, in which an attempt in flight whose recorded version or epoch is no longer current is ended without committing; Fail, in which a robot that is up stops silently, leaving any attempt in flight exactly as it was; and Return, in which a robot that stopped comes back up.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Nothing stale or unauthorised can be committed -- every attempt that is still committable, meaning its recorded version and epoch are both the current ones, belongs to a robot that still holds a credential for the current epoch.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: The optimistic scheme never livelocks -- the task board's version always eventually reaches its ceiling, so the fleet cannot spin forever beginning and abandoning attempts without any of them landing, however the robots fail and return.

---- MODULE W4Od4m3p4t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Terminals, Cars, LineBound, WaterBound, MaxTerm, NoTerminal

ASSUME NoTerminal \notin Terminals
ASSUME WaterBound <= LineBound

VARIABLES term, leader, heard, onLine, washing, override

vars == <<term, leader, heard, onLine, washing, override>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ term \in 0 .. MaxTerm
    /\ leader \in Terminals \cup {NoTerminal}
    /\ heard \in [Terminals -> 0 .. MaxTerm]
    /\ onLine \in SUBSET Cars
    /\ washing \in SUBSET Cars
    /\ override \in BOOLEAN

Init ==
    /\ term = 0
    /\ leader = NoTerminal
    /\ heard = [t \in Terminals |-> 0]
    /\ onLine = {}
    /\ washing = {}
    /\ override = FALSE

\* A superseded terminal is still there; it just is not the leader any more.
Acting(t) == leader = t /\ heard[t] = term

TakeOver(t) ==
    /\ term < MaxTerm
    /\ term' = term + 1
    /\ leader' = t
    /\ heard' = [heard EXCEPT ![t] = term + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<onLine, washing, override>>

Learn(t) ==
    /\ heard[t] < term
    /\ heard' = [heard EXCEPT ![t] = term]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, onLine, washing, override>>

Admit(t, c) ==
    /\ Acting(t)
    /\ c \notin onLine
    /\ Cardinality(onLine) < LineBound
    /\ onLine' = onLine \cup {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, heard, washing, override>>

\* The override is a way around the leadership, not around the plant.
ManagerAdmit(c) ==
    /\ override
    /\ c \notin onLine
    /\ Cardinality(onLine) < LineBound
    /\ onLine' = onLine \cup {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, heard, washing, override>>

StartWash(c) ==
    /\ c \in onLine
    /\ c \notin washing
    /\ Cardinality(washing) < WaterBound
    /\ washing' = washing \cup {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, heard, onLine, override>>

StopWash(c) ==
    /\ c \in washing
    /\ washing' = washing \ {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, heard, onLine, override>>

Exit(c) ==
    /\ c \in onLine
    /\ c \notin washing
    /\ onLine' = onLine \ {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, heard, washing, override>>

Override ==
    /\ ~override
    /\ override' = TRUE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, heard, onLine, washing>>

Cancel ==
    /\ override
    /\ override' = FALSE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, heard, onLine, washing>>

Next ==
    \/ \E t \in Terminals : TakeOver(t)
    \/ \E t \in Terminals : Learn(t)
    \/ \E t \in Terminals, c \in Cars : Admit(t, c)
    \/ \E c \in Cars : ManagerAdmit(c)
    \/ \E c \in Cars : StartWash(c)
    \/ \E c \in Cars : StopWash(c)
    \/ \E c \in Cars : Exit(c)
    \/ Override
    \/ Cancel

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Neither the conveyor nor the water plant is ever over its capacity.
CapacitiesAreNeverExceeded ==
    /\ Cardinality(onLine) <= LineBound
    /\ Cardinality(washing) <= WaterBound

CONSTANTS
    Terminals = {termA, termB}
    Cars = {car1, car2, car3}
    LineBound = 2
    WaterBound = 1
    MaxTerm = 2
    NoTerminal = noterminal

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT CapacitiesAreNeverExceeded
nl:
A car wash runs one conveyor line. Two things about it are hard limits. The line itself holds only so many cars at once -- put another car on a full line and the last one comes off the end before it is finished. Separately, the water plant only supports so many cars being actively washed at the same time; cars beyond that sit on the line waiting their turn under the arches.

Admission to the line is decided by whichever supervisor terminal is currently the leader. Leadership is carried by a term number: a terminal takes over by winding the term up and installing itself, and every terminal separately records the highest term it has heard of. A terminal only acts as leader while the term it has heard of is the current one, so a terminal that has been superseded, or that has not caught up, cannot admit anybody.

The site manager has a privileged path. With the manager override standing, a car can be put onto the line without any leader involved at all -- no term, no leadership, no terminal. What the override does not do, and this is the point, is touch either capacity: the manager's car goes onto the line only if the line has room, exactly like everybody else's. The override is a way around the leadership, not around the plant.

A car on the line may be started under the arches while the water plant has room, and stops washing when it is done. A car only comes off the end of the line once it has stopped washing.

The full set of actions is: TakeOver, in which a terminal winds the term on by one, becomes leader, and records the new term as the one it has heard of; Learn, in which a terminal behind the current term catches up to it; Admit, in which the current leader puts a car that is not on the line onto it, allowed only while the line is below its capacity; ManagerAdmit, in which, with the override standing, a car that is not on the line is put onto it with no leader involved, allowed only while the line is below its capacity; StartWash, in which a car on the line that is not washing starts washing, allowed only while the water plant is below its capacity; StopWash, in which a washing car stops; Exit, in which a car on the line that is not washing comes off the end; Override, in which the manager puts the override up; and Cancel, in which the manager takes the override down.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Neither capacity is ever exceeded -- the number of cars on the conveyor never goes above the line's capacity and the number of cars washing never goes above the water plant's capacity -- no matter how leadership changes hands, how far behind a terminal is, or whether the manager's override is standing.

---- MODULE W4Od13m1p4t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS RingSize, ShelfBound, ShelfCeiling, VanBound

ASSUME RingSize \in Nat \ {0}
ASSUME ShelfBound < ShelfCeiling

Machines == 0 .. RingSize - 1

VARIABLES token, shelf, reading, load

vars == <<token, shelf, reading, load>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ token \in Machines
    /\ shelf \in [Machines -> 0 .. ShelfCeiling]
    /\ reading \in [Machines -> 0 .. ShelfCeiling]
    /\ load \in 0 .. VanBound

Init ==
    /\ token = 0
    /\ shelf = [m \in Machines |-> 0]
    /\ reading = [m \in Machines |-> 0]
    /\ load = 0

Overfull == {m \in Machines : shelf[m] > ShelfBound}

PassToken ==
    /\ token' = (token + 1) % RingSize
    /\ UNCHANGED <<shelf, reading, load>>

\* Reading is something the van does where it is standing.
Read ==
    /\ reading[token] # shelf[token]
    /\ reading' = [reading EXCEPT ![token] = shelf[token]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, shelf, load>>

Sell(m) ==
    /\ shelf[m] > 0
    /\ shelf' = [shelf EXCEPT ![m] = @ - 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, reading, load>>

\* The franchisee can see the shelf, so it never overfills it.
TopUp(m) ==
    /\ shelf[m] < ShelfBound
    /\ shelf' = [shelf EXCEPT ![m] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, reading, load>>

\* The van cannot see the shelf, so it will not act on a stale reading.
Restock(m) ==
    /\ load > 0
    /\ reading[m] = shelf[m]
    /\ reading[m] < ShelfBound
    /\ shelf' = [shelf EXCEPT ![m] = @ + 1]
    /\ reading' = [reading EXCEPT ![m] = @ + 1]
    /\ load' = load - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED token

Reload ==
    /\ load < VanBound
    /\ load' = load + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, shelf, reading>>

Next ==
    \/ PassToken
    \/ Read
    \/ \E m \in Machines : Sell(m)
    \/ \E m \in Machines : TopUp(m)
    \/ \E m \in Machines : Restock(m)
    \/ Reload

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(Read)

\* No shelf ever holds more than it physically takes.
NoShelfIsOverfilled == Overfull = {}

StaleReadingsAreTemporary ==
    (reading[token] # shelf[token]) ~> (reading[token] = shelf[token])

====

CONSTANTS
    RingSize = 2
    ShelfBound = 1
    ShelfCeiling = 2
    VanBound = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT NoShelfIsOverfilled

PROPERTY StaleReadingsAreTemporary
nl:
A vending operator restocks its machines from a van that works a fixed round. A work token marks where the van currently is, and it moves from position to position around the round. Each machine's shelf has a hard capacity: physically only so many units fit, and pushing another one in jams the mechanism.

The depot's picture of a shelf is not the shelf. What the depot holds is a reading, taken by the van when it was last at that machine. Between visits the reading goes out of date in both directions: customers buy units out of the shelf, and the site's own franchisee tops the shelf up locally from a cupboard without telling the depot. The franchisee can see the shelf so it never overfills, but the depot cannot, and a reading that is lower than the shelf really is is exactly what would make the van push a unit into a machine that is already full.

That is why the van will not restock on an out-of-date reading. It restocks only a machine whose reading is currently equal to the shelf -- in practice, the machine it is standing at and has just read. Reading is something the van does where it is: it takes a fresh reading of whatever machine the token is at, which is what makes a stale reading a temporary condition rather than a permanent one. A machine whose reading has gone stale is not broken and nothing gives up on it; it is simply behind until the van gets to it.

The van carries a bounded load, and reloads at the depot up to that bound.

The full set of actions is: PassToken, in which the work token moves to the next position on the round; Read, in which the van takes a fresh reading of the machine the token is at, bringing the depot's reading for it into line with the shelf; Sell, in which a customer takes a unit out of a machine's shelf; TopUp, in which the site's franchisee puts a unit into a machine's shelf locally, allowed only while that shelf is below its capacity; Restock, in which the van puts a unit from its load into the shelf of a machine whose reading is equal to its shelf and whose shelf is below its capacity, bringing the reading along with it; and Reload, in which the van takes on one more unit at the depot, up to its load bound.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No shelf is ever over its capacity -- there is never a machine holding more units than the shelf physically takes, however far the depot's readings have drifted from the shelves they describe.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: A stale reading is always temporary -- whenever the depot's reading for the machine the token is at disagrees with that machine's shelf, it eventually agrees with it again.
